## Change

- [Anticipate likely changes](change/anticipate-likely-changes.md) — Method for placing interfaces: list what is likely to change (business rules, hardware, I/O formats, non-standard language features, hard design areas, status variables, sizes), give each its own class, keep the class interface free of it; effort inversely proportional to probability. Review form: find where each area's decisions are made.
- [Automated refactoring](change/automated-refactoring.md) — Concept: how far a tool-made refactoring can be trusted without running tests. A syntax-tree tool on statically resolved names most; a tool that asks a person to pick call sites, or text search-and-replace, much less; names also used through reflection or strings are where tools miss.
- [Binding time](change/binding-time.md) — A value that can change only between runs (read from a file, registry or environment) re-read at each object creation, call or redraw instead of once at load: bound later than its source changes. A load-time key with one value everywhere is over-configuration; a bare literal is named-constants-over-literals.
- [Break the build on interface change](change/break-the-build-on-interface-change.md) — A function keeps its name and signature while its meaning, unit or result convention changes, so every caller still compiles and is now wrong.
- [Do not live with broken windows](change/broken-windows.md) — A defect the code itself admits (FIXME, HACK, error dropped 'for now') stays in the region under review, neither fixed nor boarded up, or new code builds on it.
- [Change Function Declaration](change/change-function-declaration.md) — Procedure for renaming a function or changing its parameters: edit the declaration and every caller at once only when callers are few or a tool does it reliably; otherwise (many or hard-to-reach callers, a polymorphic method, a name that is not unique, a published API) extract the body into a new function, inline the old one caller by caller, then rename; for a published API, stop after extracting and deprecate the old function.
- [Code tuning procedure](change/code-tuning-procedure.md) — Use when working code is too slow and changes are being made for speed: keep a known-good version, profile to find hot spots, rule out design, data and algorithm causes, change one thing, measure it, revert anything that did not help, repeat and keep trying variants past the first win.
- [Do not refactor while adding features](change/do-not-refactor-while-adding-features.md) — One step or one diff hunk both moves or renames code and changes what it computes; a change labelled refactor alters test expectations or adds tests for new behaviour. Two single-purpose steps sharing one commit are not this sign.
- [Easier to change (ETC)](change/easier-to-change.md) — Choosing between two workable shapes for code, with no rule deciding it: prefer the one that is cheaper to change later, and if unsure make the piece replaceable.
- [Extract the scattered code before changing it everywhere](change/extract-before-changing-many-callers.md) — A change would force every client to be edited at once (a new return type, a replaced sentinel such as x == "unknown"): first extract the fragment each client repeats into one function, move callers over one at a time, and trap unexpected values while the migration runs.
- [First, do no harm](change/first-do-no-harm.md) — An added line handles a concern worse than its neighbours do: a dropped error, a bypassed check, a hard-coded value, a pasted copy, a reach across a layer.
- [Refactoring, 2nd ed. (Fowler)](change/fowler-refactoring.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: Fowler's Refactoring, 2nd ed. (English, 2018), the catalogue of behaviour-preserving changes made in small tested steps; records its authority and limits, which chapters this wiki took from, what was left out, and where it disagrees with other sources.
- [Good enough or a broken window](change/good-enough-versus-broken-window.md) — Decides whether to report a flaw in working code: a floor breach, or a page's sign with that page's conditions met, makes it a broken window; an unmet condition is reported as a question; a change of form with no named violation means stop.
- [Hide third-party APIs behind your own layer](change/hide-third-party-apis.md) — A vendor's client, query dialect or exception type named outside one adapter class, in code that also holds business logic or in the application's own signatures; application code branching on which vendor is configured, each branch calling a different API; or an adapter that hands the wrapped vendor object back out through an accessor.
- [Mechanical code transformation keeps bad logic](change/mechanical-code-transformation.md) — Concept: output of a restructuring tool, a language translator or a code generator kept and hand-maintained as if finished, though its logic is as tangled as the original's (flag variables standing in for removed jumps, meaningless names, long uniform blocks); such output is a starting point for manual refactoring, unless it is regenerated and never edited.
- [Move Function in steps](change/move-function.md) — Procedure for relocating a function whose body reaches mostly into another class, module or enclosing scope (or a nested helper that has value on its own): move the least-dependent function of a cluster first, copy and adapt, turn the original into a delegator, test, then inline the delegator.
- [Parallel change (expand-contract)](change/parallel-change.md) — Use when a rename or replacement cannot reach all its users in one change (a function called from outside this repository or by unknown clients, a stored field, a library used throughout): add the new form beside the old, keep the old as a pass-through, move users over in small steps, remove the old only when nothing uses it.
- [Parameterize with external configuration](change/parameterize-with-external-configuration.md) — Hosts, ports or tax rates as literals in source; branches on environment or customer name; a rebuild needed to change such a value. A literal that grants access is keep-secrets-out-of-source.
- [The Pragmatic Programmer, 20th Anniversary Edition](change/pragmatic-programmer.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: what the book argues and covers, which edition a citation of it means, and how to read its tips, coined terms, exercise answers and general disclaimers before relying on them.
- [Preparatory refactoring: refactor first, then add the feature](change/preparatory-refactoring.md) — A diff adds a feature or fix by copying an existing function and changing only its literal values, its output format or one step (statement copied to htmlStatement), by wrapping a condition around every line that builds output, or by fixing one of several copies; restructure first so the change lands in one place.
- [Prototype when code resists](change/prototype-when-code-resists.md) — Method for a change that keeps fighting back with no cause you can name: set the code aside and write a throwaway version until the doubt becomes a clear question. A cause you can list as constraints is find-the-real-constraints.
- [Refactor early and often](change/refactor-early-and-often.md) — Another page's finding (duplicated logic, a misleading name, a clean-up TODO) left standing on or beside lines the change touches. This page rules on when to act, not on what is wrong.
- [Refactor first, tune afterwards](change/refactor-first-tune-afterwards.md) — A structural improvement declined or reverted for speed with no measurement (a loop kept fused, a temp kept for one lookup, a split undone), justified by a comment, review remark or commit message citing performance; finish the refactoring, then measure and tune.
- [Refactor in small tested steps](change/refactor-in-small-tested-steps.md) — A large restructuring diff with no intermediate green state, structural change applied to code that no test covers, or a refactoring started or continued while a test fails instead of backing out to the last green state.
- [Refactoring warning signs (code smells)](change/refactoring-warning-signs.md) — Checklist run on a routine or class to find what to refactor: duplication, long routine or loop, poor cohesion, long parameter list, parallel edits, feature envy, overloaded primitive, tramp data, middle man, public data, subclass using little of its parent, setup/cleanup around a call, speculative code; Fowler's 24 smells (mysterious name, mutable data, loops, lazy element, temporary field, message chains, insider trading, data class, refused bequest, comments...) alongside; each routed to the page that owns it.
- [Refactoring](change/refactoring.md) — A change is refactoring only if working code keeps its observable behaviour, its internal quality rises, and it proceeds in small steps that leave the code working after each; a broad rewrite, code broken for days, a behaviour change, a change for speed at the cost of clarity, or poking at broken code under that name is not.
- [Renaming a widely used field in small steps](change/rename-widely-used-field.md) — Procedure for renaming a record field or a class's accessor pair used across a program without one big-bang edit: encapsulate, rename the private field, accept both names in the constructor, migrate callers, rename the accessors.
- [Write replaceable code instead of forecasting](change/replaceable-code-over-forecast.md) — Code justified by a future need: a comment or name citing later extension on a hook, a parameter or a one-entry registry. With no stated need, a one-occupant pattern role belongs to do-not-force-a-design-pattern, and any other single-implementation layer to know-when-to-stop where a change adds it and minimal-but-complete-functionality in code as it stands.
- [Reversibility](change/reversibility.md) — Vendor, deployment or architecture choices wired so deep that changing one means a rewrite: a decision treated as final with no seam left to reverse it.
- [Scale care to refactoring risk](change/scale-review-to-refactoring-risk.md) — A refactoring that reshapes a routine or class interface, a persisted schema or a boolean expression shares one step (one commit) with other refactorings, in a diff small enough to judge, so the risky move is not isolated.
- [Slide Statements](change/slide-statements.md) — Procedure for moving a fragment of code up or down within a function (to gather related lines before an extract, or to put a declaration by its first use) without changing behaviour: the four interference checks, CQS as the shortcut, smaller slides when a test fails.
- [Small steps with feedback](change/small-steps-with-feedback.md) — For a change too large to verify at once: establish where things stand, take the smallest step a check can judge, evaluate and repair before the next one, and split any task that needs a forecast.
- [Software entropy](change/software-entropy.md) — Why code decays: visible neglect spreads (broken windows), and small steps go unnoticed (boiled frog). The two mechanisms need different responses; only the first has a local sign in code.
- [Substitute an algorithm](change/substitute-algorithm.md) — Procedure for replacing a whole convoluted algorithm, or one duplicating a library function, with a clearer one: isolate it in one function, pin its behaviour with tests, swap, and compare outputs.
- [Keep prototype code throwaway](change/throwaway-prototype.md) — A prototype's own code has grown past the minimum its design question needed (error handling, configuration, layers, its own tests), or states no question at all; prototype code reached from the production path is tracer-code-vs-prototype.
- [Tracer code or prototype](change/tracer-code-vs-prototype.md) — A production path reads canned input or imports a spike folder: a prototype that shipped. Absent error checks or a single route only support that. A trivial routine behind a final interface is not one.
- [Tracer code](change/tracer-code.md) — A stub or trivial routine sits behind a final interface in a system still being built along one path: not a defect while it has real error handling; a stub left after the path is declared complete is dead code.
- [When to refactor](change/when-to-refactor.md) — Use when deciding whether to refactor now: before a change (preparatory), on code that took thought to understand (comprehension), on bad code passed through (litter pickup, timed by refactor-early-and-often), and not at all for ugly code nobody needs to change.
- [Where to spend refactoring effort](change/where-to-refactor.md) — Use when choosing which code to refactor: neighbours of a new routine or class, code beside a fixed defect, error-prone and high-complexity modules, code being touched anyway, and the boundary between legacy mess and clean code.

## Complexity

- [Avoid falling through case arms](complexity/avoid-case-fall-through.md) — In a C-style switch, an arm with statements but no break/return/throw that runs on into the next label with no comment or marker, or a block or loop opened under one case label and closed under another: end every arm; where fall-through is intended, mark it and say why.
- [Break and continue](complexity/break-and-continue.md) — Three or more break statements at different depths of one loop body, a continue that follows real work, an unlabelled break inside a switch or if nested in a loop, a loop body wholly wrapped in one filtering if, or a done flag threaded through a while with if-not-done guards deepening the nesting: decide between break, flags, split loops and a top-of-loop continue.
- [A cache must earn its complexity](complexity/cache-must-earn-its-complexity.md) — A function or object keeps remembered results (cachedX or lastX fields, a memo map, a lazily filled table) in front of a computation no costlier than the lookup, or with no comment, test or benchmark showing that the same inputs recur, or keyed on fewer inputs than the result depends on.
- [Case statement or if-then-else chain](complexity/case-or-if-chain.md) — A switch on a selector derived by dropping information from the real data (first letter of a command, a truncated code), so different inputs share a label; or an if-else-if chain of four or more arms, each doing different work, that tests one simple variable for equality against constants: switch on simple categorical data only, chain otherwise.
- [Choose a table access scheme](complexity/choose-table-access-scheme.md) — A lookup table of large entries mostly empty because the key's range is far wider than the entries, a table padded with duplicate rows for ranges, or a range if-chain over irregular thresholds: pick direct, indexed or stair-step access by key shape, memory and speed.
- [Class size](complexity/class-size.md) — A class body longer than the book's limit for its language, about 250 lines in Java or 100 in Ruby, counting comments and blank lines.
- [Code Complete (McConnell)](complexity/code-complete.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: McConnell's Code Complete, 2nd ed., Russian edition, a broad construction handbook whose thesis is managing complexity; records its authority and limits, which chapters this wiki took from, what was left out, and where the book disagrees with other sources.
- [Code written for the reader](complexity/code-for-the-reader.md) — Concept: code a reader must decode rather than read, kept that way on the ground that nobody else will use it; once code is shared, imported or scheduled it is public, and the book's readability work is owed before that.
- [Coding conventions as complexity control](complexity/coding-conventions.md) — Concept: code where the same kind of arbitrary decision (error reporting, resource handling, interface shape, constant marking) is made differently in each place, such as units of one kind each exposing their own ad-hoc public methods or one invariant checked in several ad-hoc forms where the language lacks an assertion helper, or a review proposing a new convention for a question the code already answers one way; a convention earns its place only by settling a question that is arbitrary but answered inconsistently.
- [Coincidental duplication](complexity/coincidental-duplication.md) — Two functions with identical bodies whose names and inputs refer to different things: decide whether they state one requirement or two before merging them.
- [Review a conditional statement](complexity/conditional-statement-checklist.md) — A procedure for reviewing if, if-else-if and case code: nominal path first, the equality boundary (> against >=), else present or explained, if and else not swapped, chain order and completeness, case selector, arm length, default and fall-through.
- [Consolidate conditional expression](complexity/consolidate-conditional-expression.md) — Two or more consecutive if-checks, or nested ifs with nothing else in the outer one, that each end in the same action or return the same value (if a return 0; if b return 0; if c return 0), written as separate tests that look independent: combine them into one condition with or/and, then name it.
- [Decision point count](complexity/decision-point-count.md) — A routine with more than 10 decision points (each if, while, repeat, for, and, or, and each case label), counted from 1: McCabe's cyclomatic measure.
- [Design pattern](complexity/design-pattern.md) — Concept: a named problem, solution and consequences; a pattern applied where its problem's conditions do not hold shows as classes named for pattern roles (Factory, Strategy, Observer, Visitor) with one implementation, one caller and nothing varying behind them.
- [Design warning signs](complexity/design-warning-signs.md) — Use as a scan before judging code: a class with more than seven members, a method with more than 10 decision points or more than three levels of nesting, code its author calls clever, or a fragment the reader has to decode rather than read; each mark is a cue to read, routed to the page that owns it.
- [Do not force code into a design pattern](complexity/do-not-force-a-design-pattern.md) — Pattern scaffolding (a factory, strategy interface, observer, visitor, or a proxy that passes every call through) with one implementation and one caller, or a diff that restructures working code into pattern roles, adding classes, while the behaviour and the number of variants stay the same.
- [Do not use the loop index after the loop](complexity/do-not-use-loop-index-after-loop.md) — Code after a for loop reads that loop's own control index (if i < MAX ...) to learn whether or where the loop stopped; set a variable named for the fact inside the loop instead.
- [Drive repeated dispatch from a table](complexity/drive-repeated-dispatch-from-a-table.md) — An if or switch chain of four or more arms over a key, all of one shape, branches nested over several enums whose every leaf assigns a constant, or an if/else-if chain of compound boolean conditions over the same few inputs (a and not c, a and b and c) whose every branch assigns a category: use a lookup table indexed by those inputs and one access or loop. Branches on a state machine's state are the state-machine pages, not this one.
- [DRY: one representation for each piece of knowledge](complexity/dry.md) — The same fact written in two places: a literal or format repeated inside a repeated expression, a copy-pasted branch differing by one operand, or a value tied to another with nothing in code linking them.
- [Estimate algorithm order](complexity/estimate-algorithm-order.md) — A nested loop or a linear search inside a loop whose bounds come from input sizes set outside the code: batch record counts, user lists, rows returned.
- [Name the intermediate object](complexity/explaining-variable.md) — A chain of two dereferences or field hops (p->next->previous), or a longer one along a single self-referential structure (node.next.previous.next), sits on the left of an assignment or inside a loop whose iterations do not change it, so the reader must reconstruct an unnamed participant; assign it to a variable named for its role.
- [Extract Variable or a function, and Inline Variable](complexity/extract-variable.md) — One return or assignment combines several unnamed sub-calculations with operators and constants, often under a comment spelling out the formula (price is base price - discount + shipping): name the parts with immutable locals, or with methods when the parts are built from an object's own fields; the other way, a local assigned once and read once whose name says no more than its expression.
- [The fastest algorithm is not always the best](complexity/fastest-algorithm-is-not-always-best.md) — A hand-written elaborate algorithm or a structure with high setup cost over a small bounded collection, or a speed-motivated change of algorithm or structure with no measured bottleneck behind it.
- [Find the real constraints](complexity/find-the-real-constraints.md) — A method for code that turned out harder than expected, with a growing pile of special cases: list what was tried, state what ruled out each path, and test whether each constraint is real. With no cause you can write down, use prototype-when-code-resists.
- [Fix performance at the level that causes it](complexity/fix-performance-at-the-right-level.md) — A slow path patched with statement-level tweaks (cached locals, unrolled loops) while its cost comes from a linear lookup or a file, network or database read inside the loop, a system call per object whose result is unused, or tracing left on in a release path.
- [For or while](complexity/for-or-while.md) — A for loop whose index is assigned inside the body to force an exit, a for over a huge literal bound used as an endless loop, a while whose counter init, test and update could sit in a for header, or an index walked only to read items[i]: pick for, while or foreach by who controls the loop.
- [goto only as a last resort, and disciplined](complexity/goto-as-last-resort.md) — A goto where an equivalent built-in construct (loop, break, return, finally, extracted routine) exists; a backward jump; several labels per routine; an unused label; a jump into the middle of another branch's block.
- [Guard clauses for error checks before the nominal path](complexity/guard-clauses.md) — The nominal work of a routine sits three or more ifs deep inside a chain of nested success checks (valid, opened, decrypted...), or inside the else of checks for unusual cases (separated, retired, capital <= 0) that each set a result variable returned at the bottom; an if/else where one leg is an unusual case rather than a normal alternative.
- [Hoist code repeated in every branch](complexity/identical-code-in-every-branch.md) — The same statement at the start or end of every branch of an if/else or every arm of a switch: move one copy out before or after the conditional.
- [Build an internal DSL from plain functions](complexity/internal-dsl-from-plain-functions.md) — Metaprogramming, macros or dynamic dispatch hooks whose only product is a nicer call surface, where every generated name could be written as an ordinary function.
- [Internal or external DSL](complexity/internal-vs-external-dsl.md) — A hand-written tokenizer or parser in the repository whose input is flat or nested key-values that YAML, JSON or CSV already express, or step matchers that only turn sentences back into calls.
- [Isolate table key computation](complexity/isolate-table-key-computation.md) — A table index computed inline (clamping with min/max, dividing into buckets, index-array lookups) at a lookup site, especially the same expression at two or more sites: move it into one named key function.
- [Keep variable live time short](complexity/keep-variable-live-time-short.md) — References to one variable spread over many lines with unrelated statements between them, nothing repeating; a block of declarations at the top of a routine far from each first use, or one long enough to need sorting; statements on two independent sets of variables interleaved (getA, getB, sumA, sumB, printA, printB) where each set could run as its own block, so a box drawn round one object's statements overlaps another's; a block of aligned assignments setting up different objects in alternation.
- [Know when to stop](complexity/know-when-to-stop.md) — A change adds an option, parameter or layer no caller needs and cites no future need, or rewrites working code with no defect and no requirement behind the rewrite.
- [Layout must tell the same story as the logic](complexity/layout-must-tell-the-same-story-as-the-logic.md) — Indentation or spacing implies a grouping the language does not apply: an unbraced if/for/while/else followed by two or more statements at the same deeper indent, an else lined up with an if it does not belong to, spacing like 3+4 * 2+7 that contradicts precedence, or an expression mixing operators of different precedence with no parentheses.
- [Lazy element](complexity/lazy-element.md) — A function whose name says no more than its body reads (lateCount(d) returning d.lateDeliveries), or a class with state whose only behaviour is one simple function used from one place: structure that adds no explanation, variation or reuse.
- [Loop as a black box](complexity/loop-as-black-box.md) — Concept: whether a reader can tell when a loop ends from its header alone, or must read the body for breaks, index assignments and flags; the idea the loop rules rest on, and which page owns each way of breaking it.
- [Loop header holds only control](complexity/loop-header-holds-only-control.md) — A for header that initializes or updates a variable the termination test does not read (a record counter), while the statement that really advances the loop sits in the body; or a loop with an empty body whose work happens inside its condition, such as while ((ch = readChar()) != EOF) ;. An empty body made visible with {} or a no-op is the book's fallback where the rewrite is not clearer (pp. 437-438).
- [Keep loop housekeeping at one end of the body](complexity/loop-housekeeping-at-one-end.md) — The per-pass updates of a loop's counters and accumulators (count++, total += ...) are scattered through the middle of its body, interleaved with the work, instead of gathered at the start or the end.
- [Keep loops short enough to see whole, and nested no more than three deep](complexity/loop-length-and-nesting.md) — A loop whose body does not fit on one screen (the book: rarely over 15-20 lines), or loops nested inside loops more than three levels deep with no if/switch among the levels (mixed nesting is tame-deep-nesting): move the inner part into routines or simplify the control; a long loop keeps one, plainly stated exit.
- [Loop with the exit in the middle](complexity/loop-with-exit-in-the-middle.md) — The same statements appear just before a loop and again at the bottom of its body (a 'loop and a half'), usually producing the value the loop condition tests; or a goto jumps into the middle of a loop on its first pass: use one unconditional loop with a single exit where the test naturally falls.
- [Managing complexity](complexity/managing-complexity.md) — Concept: the primary technical goal of design is that a reader can change one part while safely ignoring most others; code that forces many parts into mind at once fails it, whatever the local code looks like.
- [Metric outlier review](complexity/metric-outlier-review.md) — Use to choose which routines or classes to read first: count decision points, parameters, locals, lines, called routines, goto and I/O statements per unit, and how often each has been fixed, then open the units that stand far apart from their neighbours; an outlier is a cue to read, not a verdict.
- [Minimal but complete functionality](complexity/minimal-but-complete-functionality.md) — In existing code under review: a public operation, overload or endpoint no caller in the codebase reaches, a parameter every caller passes with the same value, or a branch for a mode nothing produces. In a diff, the same shapes belong to know-when-to-stop. Needs a caller search of the repository; published APIs excluded.
- [Name complex conditions](complexity/name-complex-conditions.md) — An if, else-if or while condition of three or more operands joined by and/or/not, wrapping a line or holding an inline range check, whose purpose (end reached, input valid, entry repeated) is named nowhere in the code; the same compound condition in two places; an if-else-if chain whose arms do different work and can only be told apart by reading each test; an if/else on an unnamed compound test whose legs are inline formulas: name the parts with boolean variables, the whole with a boolean function, and the legs with functions.
- [Name a repeated subexpression](complexity/name-repeated-subexpression.md) — The same non-trivial arithmetic or call subexpression, with the same operands (rate / 12 in both numerator and denominator), is written out two or more times in one statement or routine instead of being computed once into a variable named for its meaning.
- [No empty then-branch](complexity/no-empty-then-branch.md) — An if whose then-branch is empty (`;`, `pass`, `{}`) or holds only a comment, with all the work in else: negate the test, move the else body into the if, drop the else.
- [Put the nominal path first](complexity/nominal-path-first.md) — A sequence of step-then-check-status blocks whose test polarity alternates, so the normal case sits in the if at one level and in the else at the next, or a single if/else whose error branch comes first while the normal path waits in the else: put the normal case after each if and stack the error handling at the bottom.
- [One loop, one job](complexity/one-loop-one-job.md) — A single loop body that computes two or more unrelated results from the same iteration (e.g. totals and a validation report and a rewrite of the items), whose statement groups share only the loop variable.
- [Order multi-way branches deliberately](complexity/order-branches-by-frequency.md) — A switch or if-else-if chain of about ten or more arms whose labels follow no discernible order (not alphabetic or numeric, not by frequency, the one normal case buried among error codes), so finding one label means reading them all; an if chain testing a rare case first.
- [Order comparisons along the number line](complexity/order-comparisons-along-the-number-line.md) — A range test written with the variable first in both halves (i > MIN and i < MAX, x >= lo && x <= hi): rewrite as MIN <= i and i <= MAX, or i < MIN or MAX < i for outside the range.
- [Over-configuration](complexity/over-configuration.md) — Every new field bringing a config key plus admin code to store and edit it; an option switching between rival behaviours of one feature; keys holding the same value in every environment and set by nobody outside the code.
- [Functions that differ only in literal values](complexity/parameterize-function.md) — Two or more functions with the same body except for the literal numbers or strings in it (tenPercentRaise / fivePercentRaise; bottomBand / middleBand / topBand over hard-coded boundaries); merge them into one function taking the literals as parameters.
- [Prefer positive conditions](complexity/prefer-positive-conditions.md) — An if/else whose condition is a negation (if !ok … else …), a double negative such as !notFound, or several not-operators in one test: swap the branches, rename the flag positively, or apply De Morgan.
- [Do not tune code without a measurement](complexity/premature-code-tuning.md) — Statement-level tricks for speed (pointer walking instead of indexing, a hand-unrolled loop with a tail fix-up, a loop duplicated per branch of an invariant test, a sentinel written past an array's end, a running accumulator instead of index multiplication, a precomputed table or bit trick in place of a plain computation, juggled loop indexes) with no profile naming it a hot spot and no resource target on it, while the algorithm itself is unchanged.
- [Program close to the problem domain](complexity/program-close-to-the-domain.md) — The same call sequence repeated four or more times with no branch on a key and only literals changing, together stating one table of facts such as routes, rules or test cases.
- [Remove calls you cannot justify](complexity/remove-calls-you-cannot-justify.md) — A run of near-synonymous calls on one object with nothing between them (refresh, redraw, flush, sync), left in because the result finally looked right.
- [Remove dead code](complexity/remove-dead-code.md) — Commented-out code, a private or file-local function or constant with no callers, a branch whose condition can never hold, or code after an unconditional return: delete it and rely on version control to bring it back.
- [Replace inline code with an existing function call](complexity/replace-inline-code-with-function-call.md) — A block of statements inside a routine computes what an existing function in scope (the project's own or a library's) already computes, such as a hand-written max loop where max exists: call the function, unless its name would read wrong in that place, which shows the likeness is coincidental.
- [Speculative generality](complexity/speculative-generality.md) — Concept: hooks, parameters, abstract classes or delegation added for a need that nothing has yet (an abstract class with one trivial subclass, an unused or always-constant parameter, a pass-through delegating method or class, a function whose only callers are tests); each shape is routed to the page that owns it.
- [Stair-step lookup boundaries](complexity/stair-step-lookup-boundaries.md) — A range-to-category lookup loop over a bounds array where the comparison (< vs <=) does not match the stated ranges, the top range has no bound or sentinel, or values at the boundaries are untested.
- [Stop a loop once the answer is known](complexity/stop-loop-once-answer-known.md) — A search loop that sets a found-flag (or records a position) and keeps iterating to the end of the collection although nothing after the first hit can change the result, and no break, return or flag test in the condition ends it: exit at the first hit.
- [Structured programming](complexity/structured-programming.md) — Concept: control constructs with one entry and one exit; any control flow can be built from sequence, selection and iteration, so break, continue, return and throw are each examined for whether they make the flow easier to follow.
- [Tame deep nesting](complexity/tame-deep-nesting.md) — if/switch blocks nested more than three or four levels inside one routine, alone or inside a loop, with long bodies between levels, or nested ifs whose inner test re-narrows a range the outer one already fixed (q > 10, then q > 100, then q > 1000).
- [Use existing components before writing your own](complexity/use-existing-components-before-writing-your-own.md) — A hand-written container, sort, search, or date/number/format routine duplicates what the standard library or a dependency already in the project provides, with no stated speed, precision or interface need.

## Debugging

- [After a surprising bug](debugging/after-a-surprising-bug.md) — Use once a defect is fixed but nothing else moved: the fix was not rerun against the diagnosis tests, no test now catches it, bad data still travels layers before failing, and the same defect may sit elsewhere.
- [Binary search debugging](debugging/binary-search-debugging.md) — Use when a failure sits in a long stack trace, a large failing input, a large region of code or an unknown change across releases, and candidates are being checked one by one; or a new defect appeared after an edit and looks unrelated to it, and nobody has diffed against the last working version.
- [Check loop boundaries by hand](debugging/check-loop-boundaries-by-hand.md) — A loop bug 'fixed' by flipping < to <= or adding or subtracting 1 from an index until a test passes, with no walk through the first, a middle and the last iteration.
- [Debugging procedure](debugging/debugging-procedure.md) — Use when a failure's cause is unknown and fixes are being tried by guess: an edit made before the failure was reproduced or the wrong value seen, a hypothesis that ignores some observations, a fix chosen while several causes remain open, or a warning-laden build under investigation.
- [Do not silence warnings](debugging/do-not-silence-warnings.md) — A compiler or analyser warning is suppressed by a pragma, annotation or lowered warning level with no stated reason, or a change adds a warning to the build and leaves it there.
- [Failing test before the fix](debugging/failing-test-before-the-fix.md) — A test added with a bug fix also passes against the unfixed code, or the reproduction exists only as manual steps in a ticket. A bug-fix diff with no test at all is find-bugs-once.
- [Fix the model, not the offset](debugging/fix-the-model-not-the-offset.md) — A literal +1 or -1 applied to a value received from elsewhere with no named reason, often paired with an opposite adjustment in another function.
- [Fix the root cause, not the symptom](debugging/fix-the-root-cause.md) — A guard, clamp, default or catch is added at the line where a failure surfaced, or a branch keyed on one input value (a client id, a magic argument) overwrites a computed result, while the code that produces the bad value stays unchanged.
- [Mental set in debugging](debugging/mental-set-in-debugging.md) — Concept: why a reader overlooks a defect in plain sight (mental set) and why a region set aside early can be the one holding it; the code shapes it explains are owned by layout-must-tell-the-same-story-as-the-logic and names-differ-by-more-than-a-character.
- [One change at a time](debugging/one-change-at-a-time.md) — A bug-fix diff bundles two or more independent edits, each of which could plausibly explain the fixed symptom, so nobody can say which one fixed it or whether one introduced a look-alike defect.
- [Perturbing system state to expose hidden defects](debugging/perturb-state-to-expose-uninitialized-data.md) — Procedure for a program that fails once in a hundred runs on the same input, which usually means it reads uninitialised state: fill memory with non-zero patterns, fail allocations, check bounds, so the failure happens every time.
- [Programming by coincidence](debugging/programming-by-coincidence.md) — Concept: code whose author cannot say why it works; owns a change kept because it made a run pass, with no stated cause, and names the owners of the boundary, offset and leftover-call shapes.
- [Prove it, don't assume it](debugging/prove-dont-assume.md) — A routine on the failing path is passed over because it is tested or long-used, though its tests never use the failing data, context or boundary.
- [Random failures: suspect concurrency](debugging/random-failures-suspect-concurrency.md) — Failures that appear at arbitrary places, between runs, with symptoms that contradict the state on disk, often after work became concurrent: look for what the failing code shares, including process-wide state.
- [Check the resource balance](debugging/resource-balance-check.md) — For a suspected leak or a long-running loop: wrap each resource type, count allocations and releases, and assert usage has not grown at a fixed point.
- [Rewrite an erratic method instead of patching it](debugging/rewrite-a-method-you-do-not-understand.md) — Two or more special-case branches in one method, keyed to particular input values, that correct the result its general path already computed (often with comments naming bugs); decide rewrite from pseudocode over another patch.
- [select isn't broken](debugging/select-isnt-broken.md) — A sleep, retry, reimplementation or comment works around a library, OS or compiler call, blaming it with no link to a reproduced defect in that dependency.
- [Stabilize the error](debugging/stabilize-the-error.md) — Use when a failure appears only sometimes, or the only reproduction is a large scenario with many inputs: make it occur reliably, then strip the test until every remaining factor changes the outcome.
- [Logging execution in terms of states](debugging/state-machine-execution-log.md) — Logic with complex behaviour debugged from print statements scattered through branch and action bodies, when a trace of the state machine's own steps (state before, event, inputs the guards read, transition taken, outputs, state after, nested machines indented) could be written at the one transition function.
- [Build debug aids in early and make them switchable](debugging/switchable-debug-aids.md) — Debug checks sit commented out, or behind a constant edited by hand in source (`DEBUG = true`, `if false`), instead of behind one build-configured switch or a check routine with a full and an empty implementation.
- [Test window into running code](debugging/test-window.md) — A long-running component writes a counter or status field that no accessor, endpoint or log line reads, or a comment says to attach a debugger to see it, so nothing outside the process can read its state.
- [Time-box quick debugging](debugging/timebox-quick-debugging.md) — Use when a debugging session has run far longer than the code took to write, or hours have gone into one approach with no progress: set a time limit for the current approach, then brainstorm alternatives and switch, to a brute-force method certain to converge, a rewrite of the fragment, or a design that removes the problem.
- [Trace id across messages](debugging/trace-id-across-messages.md) — Message types and handler log lines carry no identifier copied from the incoming message to the outgoing ones: in an actor or message-driven flow the path of one request cannot be rebuilt from the logs.
- [Trace statements in a uniform format](debugging/trace-statements.md) — Diagnostic output differs in format at each call site, or only one side of a paired event such as open/close is traced, so a log cannot be processed by a tool.
- [Where defects come from](debugging/where-defects-come-from.md) — Concept: defect-origin figures that rank suspects in a search: most fixes touch one routine, construction defects are the programmer's own far more than the compiler's or OS's, one-character typos are common and costly, misread design is frequent.

## Documentation

- [Comment what a declaration's name cannot carry](documentation/comment-data-declarations.md) — A local variable for a length, time, angle or amount carries no unit in its name, type or comment, so an assignment can join two quantities in different units unseen; a bit-flag word has no documented layout; a global has no stated role.
- [Kinds of comments](documentation/comment-kinds.md) — Concept: every comment repeats the code, explains it, marks unfinished work, summarises, states intent, or holds what code cannot; only the last three belong in finished code, and the test is whether the comment restates the lines it sits on one by one, at their own level, or says in a sentence what several lines together achieve.
- [Comment why, not how](documentation/comment-why-not-how.md) — A comment restates the code under it in language terms ('if flag is zero'), explains a literal a named constant could carry, lists the same steps or numbers as the body, contradicts it, or sits as a template on every function, while a surprising delay, ordering, workaround or deliberate non-obvious technique has no stated reason.
- [Record key design decisions in file and class headers](documentation/design-notes-in-code-headers.md) — A file or class header only restates its name or lists members, or is missing, while the body holds a choice it never names (a cache, chunked or lazy processing, an unexpected data structure, a departure from sibling units): say what the unit hides, why it is arranged so, and which alternative was rejected.
- [Documentation examples come from tested code](documentation/doc-examples-from-tested-code.md) — A code sample in a document or docstring is a hand-pasted copy, with no include directive and no test running it, so it can drift from the code it shows.
- [Consider the else, and say why it is absent](documentation/document-the-missing-else.md) — An if with no else whose false case is a real input and not obviously a no-op (input validation, range or status checks), with nothing near it saying what happens then: add an else that handles it, or a comment saying the false case is deliberately ignored.
- [Keep documentation in the source](documentation/documentation-in-the-source.md) — An exported function or module has no doc comment, its contract lives only in a separate file, or its doc comment names a parameter the signature no longer has.
- [Avoid end-of-line comments](documentation/end-of-line-comments.md) — A trailing comment restates its own line, sits on a block header so it is unclear how many lines it covers, records a bug number, date and initials, or marks the end of a long nested block.
- [Use a comment style that is easy to change](documentation/maintainable-comment-style.md) — A comment's decoration has to be realigned by hand when its text changes: dot leaders between a name and its meaning, a right-hand border of asterisks, a dashed rule ending in a plus, or a column of line comments over long prose.
- [Standardise marker comments](documentation/marker-comments.md) — A to-do marker sits beside a stub result that callers reach, or one codebase mixes several marker notations (TODO, ****, !!!, TBD), so a mechanical search before release misses some.
- [Rewrite tricky code instead of commenting it](documentation/rewrite-tricky-code.md) — A comment warns that the code below is tricky, fragile or must not be touched ('IMPORTANT', 'do not change', 'clever'), explains a trick a plain construct would avoid, or carries the only statement of a lifetime dependency between two objects.
- [Keep routine headers brief and near the code](documentation/routine-header-comment.md) — A routine carries a fixed-field header block (Name, Purpose, Algorithm, Inputs, History, Author) out of scale with its body, its purpose line joins unrelated actions, or a parameter it writes to is declared like the ones it only reads.
- [Self-documenting code](documentation/self-documenting-code.md) — Concept: code whose meaning a reader recovers only from a comment, or not at all (one-letter counters, a flag array named for a criterion rather than what it holds, loops whose ends cannot be seen) is repaired by names and structure, not by more comments.
- [Source code as the authoritative description](documentation/source-code-as-the-authoritative-description.md) — Concept: the code is the one description of a program that stays current, so a fact a maintainer needs belongs in names, types, constants and reason-giving comments, not only in a document beside the code.
- [State the contract of a routine](documentation/state-the-contract.md) — The body indexes, divides or dereferences an argument under a condition (non-empty, positive, open) that its comment and signature never state.
- [Tests instead of documentation](documentation/tests-instead-of-documentation.md) — A doc comment on a class or method declaration carries the meaning its names lack (`Helper.saveAndCheck`, `convert(int, boolean)`): rename until the comment is redundant, and let a unit test show the use.

## Errors

- [Against Railway-Oriented Programming (Wlaschin, 2019)](errors/against-railway-oriented-programming.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: the author's own critique of his 2013 article, listing when not to return a result type (diagnostics needed, reinventing try/catch, fail fast, private control flow, nobody cares about the reason, I/O, performance, interop) and splitting errors into domain errors, panics and infrastructure errors.
- [Keep array indexes in bounds, in order and uncrossed](errors/array-index-discipline.md) — An index computed by arithmetic with no length check, a loop over an array compared with <= against its length or bounded by a hard-coded number, a multidimensional access a[i][j] where a[j][i] was meant, or nested loops where one index leaks into the other's position.
- [Assert what cannot happen](errors/assert-the-impossible.md) — A comment claims a run-time fact (never null, always sorted, can't happen) with no check beside it, an impossible branch is empty, a multi-way branch over a closed set has no default arm, a file operation has no failure path because it cannot fail, logic relies on a + 1 > a, a field set by program logic is silently mishandled outside a sub-range (a negative discount rate) and checked nowhere, or a hand-written algorithm's result goes unchecked.
- [Assert, then handle the error anyway](errors/assert-then-handle-anyway.md) — A routine both asserts a condition on its arguments and, right after, handles the same violation at run time (clamps, rejects); decide whether that double check is warranted or whether one of the two should go.
- [Assertion or error handling](errors/assertion-or-error-handling.md) — An assert or precondition guards a value just read from a user, file, network or config; this page also decides whether a soft error return covers a state only a bug can produce.
- [Assertion conditions have no side effects](errors/assertion-side-effects.md) — The condition inside an assert advances an iterator, pops, increments, assigns or writes, so the check changes what the program does.
- [Attack surface](errors/attack-surface.md) — Every entry and exit point of a program counts against it: complex code, external input, unauthenticated services, disclosing output and exposed debug information.
- [Barricade: validate at the boundary, assume inside](errors/barricade.md) — Raw external values reach internal routines unchecked (including a server handler that stores a request field because the client form already checked it), or the opposite: private helpers re-validate and repair the same parameter the public entry already checked, so no one place is the boundary of trusted data.
- [The caller owns the precondition](errors/caller-owns-the-precondition.md) — A routine clamps, coerces or defaults an out-of-domain argument at entry, or holds the caller's decision about what to do with bad input.
- [Chain exceptions](errors/chain-exceptions.md) — A catch block throws a new exception built from a message alone, without passing the caught exception as its cause, so the low-level reason is lost; or a library throws or demands catching the language's root exception class.
- [Collect the failures of independent validations](errors/collect-independent-validation-failures.md) — Several checks of one input that do not depend on each other are chained so the first failure ends the chain (early returns, or bind between validation steps), and that one failure goes back to the person who must correct the input, who then fixes errors one round trip at a time.
- [Composite resource](errors/composite-resource.md) — Several acquisitions in a row followed by `if a and b`, or nested try/rescue with a give_back per resource, in the caller: partial acquisition leaks resources and the business logic disappears behind cleanup.
- [One error-handling strategy per application](errors/consistent-error-handling-strategy.md) — Peer modules of one layer, or the functions of one module, signal the same kind of failure by different mechanisms (one returns a code or null, one throws, one clamps, one shows a dialog), the same input is validated at its entry in one module and nowhere in its peer, or user-facing error messages are composed in many places across domain code.
- [Contract of a method whose behaviour depends on control state](errors/contract-of-state-dependent-method.md) — A client-facing postcondition, docstring or test that names a class's private control state ("if in state 2, the alarm hours increase") leaks the state to clients and over-specifies; a per-state branch that does what the method's general contract excludes breaks it, as a weakening override would.
- [Crash early](errors/crash-early.md) — An impossible branch logs or returns a default and carries on, a catch swallows the failure, or a failure only a bug can produce returns a sentinel such as NaN or -1 that flows onward.
- [The default branch catches the unexpected](errors/default-branch-catches-the-unexpected.md) — A multi-way branch over a closed set with no final else or no default, so an unplanned value falls through silently; or a switch/chain whose default or last else does the work of one nameable value (the last enum member, the last command letter): list every expected case and make default/else report an internal error.
- [Which defensive code stays in production](errors/defensive-code-in-production.md) — A release build keeps a debug-time abort that can lose the user's unsaved work, drops a check on a calculation whose error would go unnoticed, or shows the user a message written for the developer; decide per check what the release keeps, removes or turns into a log entry.
- [Design by contract](errors/design-by-contract.md) — A routine's rights and duties stated as preconditions, postconditions and invariants; relevant when a body assumes what no signature, comment, test or check states, or when a mutator's conditions still let a class invariant break.
- [Distrust external input](errors/distrust-external-input.md) — A value from a request, a file or a user is concatenated into a shell command, a query or markup without being sanitized first, or a secret is silently cut or stripped before hashing or storing.
- [Do not disclose through output](errors/do-not-disclose-in-output.md) — A stack trace reaches a user-facing response, an error reveals another account's state, a full identifier is returned or a diagnostic route has no access check.
- [Do not implement cryptography yourself](errors/do-not-implement-cryptography.md) — A hand-written cipher, a home-made hash or salt scheme, MD5 or SHA-1 for passwords, or login and password storage built from primitives.
- [Several error exits that share one cleanup](errors/error-exits-sharing-cleanup.md) — A routine that acquires something, runs several steps that can each fail, and must release it on every exit: shown as goto to a cleanup label, deep nested ifs, repeated 'if status == OK' checks, or the release copied before each early return.
- [Throw exceptions at the interface's level of abstraction](errors/exception-at-the-interface-abstraction.md) — A domain-level method declares or lets escape a low-level exception from its implementation (an end-of-file, socket, SQL or disk error from a getter like get_tax_id), so callers depend on how the class stores its data.
- [An exception carries the data that caused it](errors/exception-message-carries-context.md) — A throw passes a fixed message ("index out of range", "invalid value") without the offending value and the bounds or state it was checked against, so whoever reads the report cannot tell why it fired.
- [Release resources safely under exceptions](errors/exception-safe-release.md) — A resource is acquired inside a try whose finally releases it; its release sits after the use with no finally or scope binding; or a class holding a file, stream or connection has no close protocol, or leaves release to a finalizer or the garbage collector.
- [Throw only for truly exceptional situations](errors/exceptions-for-the-exceptional.md) — A catch wrapped round a single call, to an exception the callee throws for an ordinary outcome (not found, end of input, invalid entry), whose body returns a normal result or chooses the next step; or a throw-catch pair inside one routine used as a goto.
- [Failure atomicity](errors/failure-atomicity.md) — A method assigns one field and then reaches a check or call that can throw before assigning the rest, so a failure leaves the object half-updated; or the code saves fields to temporaries to roll back by hand.
- [Fault, error, failure](errors/fault-error-failure.md) — Concept: three terms for one misbehaviour, each a different place to act: the fault is the cause in the code or configuration (fixed in source), the error is its manifestation in the running system (detected or not), the failure is the service that is not delivered (handled by a fallback); a handler that swallows a failure turns a detected error back into an undetected one.
- [Fault-tolerance techniques](errors/fault-tolerance-techniques.md) — Concept: the options for keeping a computation working after a fault (retry from a known-good state, auxiliary code, voting among implementations, substitute values, degraded mode, shutdown, restart) and what each costs in code.
- [Guard before the guarded operand](errors/guard-before-the-guarded-operand.md) — A condition that indexes, divides or dereferences before the check that makes it safe (item[i] != 0 and i < MAX; x/d > m && d != 0), or puts the guard under an operator or call that evaluates every operand: put the guard first under a short-circuit and, or nest the test.
- [Handle errors in the stages or in the pipeline](errors/handle-errors-in-stages-or-in-the-pipeline.md) — The same pass-through check, if input is failure return it, repeated at the top of several stages or between them; each stage accepts a wrapper though it works only on the unwrapped value; or a stage that cannot fail returns success(...) on every path only to fit the chain.
- [Isolate unsafe memory operations behind wrappers](errors/isolate-unsafe-memory-operations.md) — In code that manages memory by hand, raw allocation and release calls or link-field updates (p->next = ...) appear at many sites with no wrapper or owning routine that checks, poisons and nulls; a loop frees a node and then reads its next; a pointer is declared far from its allocation.
- [Keep secrets out of source and plain text](errors/keep-secrets-out-of-source.md) — A key, token or password appears as a literal in source or a committed config, or a credential column stores readable text.
- [Least privilege](errors/least-privilege.md) — Code holds elevated rights from entry to exit when only one call needs them, a service uses administrator credentials, or a single admin/user flag guards every resource.
- [Leave assertions on in production](errors/leave-assertions-on.md) — A release build, flag or macro switches all assertions off, or checks sit inside a debug-only guard, instead of disabling only the check that really hurts performance.
- [Do not catch only to log and rethrow](errors/log-and-rethrow.md) — A handler whose body only logs a message and rethrows the same exception, often repeated once per exception type.
- [Never return null](errors/never-return-null.md) — A method declared to return an object returns null (None, nil) on a not-found path, and its callers compare the result with null before using it.
- [Do not accept NULL as an argument](errors/no-null-arguments.md) — A method branches on `param == null` to pick a behaviour ("if mask is null, return all files"), or its contract documents null as a meaningful value of a parameter.
- [Offensive programming: make errors loud during development](errors/offensive-programming.md) — A default or else arm for an unexpected case, or an assertion handler, lets the program continue silently or after a keypress in development builds, so a known problem can be skipped instead of fixed.
- [Quality characteristics and their trade-offs](errors/quality-characteristics-trade-offs.md) — Concept: quality goals conflict; code tuned for correctness halts on bad input, code tuned for robustness carries on, and code written with no stated priority optimizes whatever the request happened to stress.
- [Railway oriented programming (Wlaschin, 2013)](errors/railway-oriented-programming.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: a web article on chaining result-returning functions (success or failure) with a small set of adapters (bind, map, tee, a catching adapter, parallel validation), whose pages here own the chained pass-through check, a stage that cannot fail wrapped only to fit a chain, and independent validations that stop at the first failure.
- [Recover only at entry points](errors/recover-only-at-entry-points.md) — A catch below an entry point does not rethrow: it returns 0, -1 or a default, assigns a fallback value, or only logs, for a failure a correct program can meet (I/O, network, parsing external text); or the reverse, an entry point or main loop with no handler around the unit of work while the user's unsaved data lives in memory.
- [Release a lock on every path](errors/release-lock-on-every-path.md) — `lock()` and `unlock()` as plain statements in one body with a call that can raise, or a return, between them: an exception or early return leaves the lock held and later callers hang.
- [Rely only on documented behaviour](errors/rely-only-on-documented-behaviour.md) — A caller passes a value outside a routine's stated input, or depends on an order, format or side result the routine never promised.
- [Robustness versus correctness](errors/robustness-versus-correctness.md) — A bad value is replaced by a neutral value, the last value, the nearest legal value or the next record in code whose wrong output is costly (a dose, an account, a tax figure); a guard swaps an illegal operand for one chosen only so the next operation succeeds (if hours == 0, hours = 1); or cosmetic code aborts the program on a glitch it could absorb.
- [Safety counter](errors/safety-counter.md) — A loop in critical code that walks a linked structure or waits on an external condition with no bound on its iterations; or, the reverse, a lone safety counter in one loop that no project standard requires.
- [Secure defaults](errors/secure-defaults.md) — An option's default is its less safe value, such as verification off or debug on, so the caller has to opt in to safety.
- [Semantic invariant](errors/semantic-invariant.md) — A fixed requirement that decides what every failure path must do, as distinct from a policy that may change; check retries and recovery branches against it.
- [Accept strictly, promise little](errors/strict-accept-narrow-promise.md) — A routine opens by normalising several shapes of the same argument, or returns success values of different kinds on different paths, such as one item or a list. A declared success-or-failure result is not this sign.
- [Guard peer routines to one robustness level](errors/uniform-robustness-level.md) — Peer routines or classes in one module calling the same dependency are guarded very unevenly (one wraps the call in retries, timeouts and a fallback, its neighbour calls it bare), with no requirement or comment behind the difference.
- [Validate exchanged data against a declared schema and reject it, rather than guess](errors/validate-exchanged-data-against-a-declared-schema.md) — Code reading a document from another system (file, message, payload) only parses it and then reads fields off the result, or fills a missing required field with a default (`or ""`, `.get(key, 0)`), instead of checking it against one declared structure and rejecting a non-conforming document with an error naming what is missing.
- [Wrap values passed between transformations](errors/wrap-values-between-transformations.md) — A fallible routine returns a bare value and signals an expected failure by null, -1 or an empty string, so its declared result hides that it can fail; or the reverse, a result type used in place of exceptions: a catch-all turning any exception into a failure value, a failure holding a caught exception or stack trace, a failure type listing every way an I/O call can fail.

## Functions

- [Combine Functions into Transform](functions/combine-functions-into-transform.md) — The same derived values are computed from a source record in several clients, and the record is not changed afterwards: one enrich/transform function deep-copies the record and adds every derived field, without altering its input; a client that later assigns to a source field of the enriched record leaves its derived fields stale.
- [A method either builds or manipulates, never both](functions/command-query-separation.md) — A method or function that changes state and also returns a value (bytes written, a 'changed' flag, the previous value, the new value it just set, as roll() returning the face value; or a finder that also raises an alarm, as alertForMiscreant returning the name it found); split it into a command and a query, or return an operation object.
- [Decompose a requirement into transformations](functions/decompose-into-transformations.md) — Procedure for a function that tangles several conversions: name input and output, list the stages with sample data, split any stage too big to write directly, then compose.
- [Do not inline routines by hand for speed](functions/do-not-hand-inline-for-speed.md) — A small routine's body copied by hand into several callers, with speed given in a comment as the reason ("inlined for performance") and no measurement showing that the call costs anything.
- [Do not reuse parameters as working variables](functions/do-not-reuse-parameters-as-working-variables.md) — A routine assigns to its own input parameter (x = x * factor) and reads it again afterwards, so below that line the parameter's name no longer holds what the caller passed.
- [Make every path of a function set its return value](functions/every-path-sets-the-return-value.md) — A function with several branches or early exits where one path reaches the end without assigning or returning a value, relying on an implicit default or a left-over variable.
- [Extract Function: the mechanics](functions/extract-function.md) — Procedure for moving a fragment of a long function into its own function without breaking it: name it for what it does, sort the fragment's locals into read-only (parameters, including a structure mutated in place), one modified (return it, initialise it inside), and accumulators (shadow and return); abandon or simplify first when many locals are assigned or several values must come out; extract to sibling level when the function will move elsewhere.
- [Extract a routine to name a step, however small](functions/extract-routine-to-name-a-step.md) — An inline loop or pair of order-dependent statements whose result has a nameable meaning (find the leaf, pop the stack) sits in the middle of a longer routine, or one intent comment heads far more than ten lines; move it into a routine named for that meaning.
- [Finish what you start](functions/finish-what-you-start.md) — A resource is opened in one routine and closed in another, shared through a field the orchestrating routine never mentions, so an added branch skips the close.
- [Function or command object](functions/function-or-command-object.md) — A long function whose locals are so entangled that Extract Function would need most of them as parameters, so it is turned into an object with an execute method; or, the other way, a small class built and called once per use (new ChargeCalculator(a, b, c).charge) with no undo, queueing, staged setup or subclassing, which is just a function in disguise.
- [Use a function only when returning its named value is the point](functions/function-or-procedure.md) — A call to a mutating routine and the test of its returned status are fused in one condition (if report.FormatOutput(r) == Success) in a project that reports failure through return values: split the call from the test.
- [Inline Function: the mechanics](functions/inline-function.md) — Procedure for putting a function's body back into its callers and deleting it: check it is not polymorphic, replace one call at a time and test, move statement by statement when the body does not paste in cleanly; do not attempt it on recursion, several returns or another object's internals. Also the first step of re-factoring a badly split group of functions or a chain of pure delegations.
- [Inside-out loop construction](functions/inside-out-loop-construction.md) — A procedure for writing a hard loop correctly the first time: code one action with constants, wrap it in a loop, replace constants with indexes, add initialization last.
- [Keep each case arm short](functions/keep-case-arms-short.md) — A case or switch arm holding many lines of its own logic (a loop, a nested if, more than about five lines) so the labels of the branch cannot be seen together: move the arm's body into a routine named for the action and call it.
- [Limit a routine to about seven parameters](functions/limit-parameter-count.md) — A routine (not a constructor) declares clearly more than seven parameters: the routine is too tightly coupled to its callers.
- [Make input-only parameters visible in the signature](functions/mark-input-only-parameters.md) — A signature leaves its input-only parameters unmarked although the language or project has a read-only marker (const, final, readonly, an agreed prefix) used elsewhere in the code, or a parameter carrying that marker or prefix appears on the left of an assignment or as the receiver of a mutating call.
- [Make argument-to-parameter matching checkable](functions/match-arguments-to-parameters.md) — A call passes several adjacent arguments of the same quantity positionally (Transfer(from, to, amount) with two account ids, Move(srcId, dstId)), so swapping two compiles and runs.
- [Move statements across the call boundary](functions/move-statements-across-call-boundary.md) — The same statements immediately before or after every call of a function (move them into it), or a parameter that only skips or alters the function's first or last statement for some callers, or a caller that overwrites what the callee's last statement produced right after the call (move that statement out to the callers).
- [One side effect per statement](functions/one-side-effect-per-statement.md) — An expression that changes a variable (++, --, an assignment, a mutating call) and also reads that same variable elsewhere in the same expression, such as print(++n, n + 2) or values[i++] + values[i], or packs several mutations into one expression; a side effect in a loop condition is loop-header-holds-only-control.
- [Pass a value or let the function find it](functions/parameter-or-query.md) — A call passes a value the callee could compute from another of its parameters or from its own fields (order.discountedPrice(base, order.discountLevel)); or, the other way, a method meant to be referentially transparent reads a mutable object it reaches through a field, so the same call returns different results: move the value out of or into the parameter list.
- [Order parameters input, modified, output](functions/parameter-order.md) — A parameter list mixing read-only inputs, in-out parameters and outputs in no order, a status or error output that is not last, or related routines taking the same parameters in different positions.
- [Pass what the routine uses, or the whole object](functions/pass-what-the-routine-uses.md) — A routine takes a whole domain object but reads only one or two of its fields, so a caller that holds those values elsewhere must create or fake the object to call it; a caller fills an object by setters only to make one call and copies its fields back after; or, the other way, every caller passes several fields of one object in the same positions (low = r.range.low; high = r.range.high; plan.withinRange(low, high)), or an object passes several of its own fields to another object: decide by what abstraction the routine's interface forms.
- [Programs transform data](functions/programs-transform-data.md) — Design that starts from classes and modules instead of asking what goes in, what comes out and which stages lie between; shows as logic organised around holders of data rather than around the flow.
- [Pseudocode Programming Process](functions/pseudocode-programming-process.md) — Procedure for writing a non-trivial routine: state its contract, write intent-level pseudocode, turn it into comments, fill code under each, then desk-check, polish and iterate; the polish step is a short review of a routine just written.
- [Recursion or iteration](functions/recursion-or-iteration.md) — A routine recursing over a linear sequence where each call does one step and makes one self-call (factorial, Fibonacci, summing a list): a loop is clearer. Backtracking or branching search is where recursion pays.
- [Recursion must provably stop and stay within one routine](functions/recursion-safeguards.md) — A recursive routine with no base-case test reached before the self-call, with no visited-set on a graph or grid walk, or recursing through a cycle of routines (A calls B calls A).
- [Remove a loop accumulator in four steps](functions/remove-loop-accumulator.md) — Procedure for a variable initialised before a loop and added to on each pass (volumeCredits += ..., total += ...) alongside other work in the same body: split the loop, slide the initialisation down, extract the total into a function, inline the variable.
- [Remove parameters the routine does not use](functions/remove-unused-parameters.md) — A declared parameter the body never reads (screenX, screenY passed and ignored), or an output parameter the body never assigns.
- [Replace a loop with a collection pipeline](functions/replace-loop-with-pipeline.md) — A loop whose whole body selects, transforms or accumulates one collection (an accumulator declared before it, a first-time flag or continue that skips items, an if that filters, a local that reshapes the item, an append or a running total), in a language or project that has first-class functions and filter/map/reduce.
- [Replace a temp with a query before extracting](functions/replace-temp-with-query.md) — Inside a long function about to be split, a local assigned once from a lookup or expression on values every fragment already has (play = plays[perf.playID]) and read in the fragments to be extracted, so each extraction carries it as an extra parameter beside the value it derives from (amountFor(perf, play)); or the same derivation computed into locals in several methods of one class.
- [Resource acquisition and release order](functions/resource-acquisition-order.md) — Two code paths take the same locks or resources in different orders, or resources that refer to each other are released in the order they were acquired.
- [Give each routine functional cohesion](functions/routine-cohesion.md) — A routine whose operations share only an execution order, the same data, the moment they run, or a control flag that picks one of several unrelated actions (InputAll(kind), Startup doing the work itself); split it into routines that each do one thing.
- [Let complexity, not a line count, limit routine length](functions/routine-length.md) — A routine over 200 non-blank, non-comment lines, or code split into Part1/Part2 pieces only to meet a fixed line limit: judge the length by cohesion, nesting depth, variable count and decision points, not by a quota.
- [Review a routine against the routine checklist](functions/routine-review-checklist.md) — Procedure for auditing one routine: reason for existing, cohesion, name, coupling, length, then each parameter's use, order, mode, count and documented assumptions, then every return path; worked on a routine with eleven parameters and a dozen defects.
- [Similar functions with a varying middle](functions/similar-functions-varying-middle.md) — Two or more functions share the same opening and closing lines and differ only in the algorithm between them.
- [Split Phase: separate two stages joined by an intermediate record](functions/split-phase.md) — Procedure for a function whose first part works on one set of inputs and whose later part works on another (pricing from product data, then shipping from shipping data; or calculation, then rendering), the halves linked only by a few locals: move the second part into its own function, pass it an intermediate record built by the first, then extract the first.
- [Tramp data](functions/tramp-data.md) — A parameter that a routine never reads itself and only hands on to the next call, repeated across two or more levels of a call chain.
- [Prefer a transformation pipeline to a method chain](functions/transformation-pipeline-over-method-chain.md) — A chain of three or more calls that convert data, each receiver being the differently typed object the previous call returned: pass each result to a free function instead.

## Naming

- [Abbreviate only when forced, and then consistently and pronounceably](naming/abbreviation-discipline.md) — Shortened words where full words would fit: one word abbreviated two ways (Num/No, cust/customer), a word missing one letter (indx), unpronounceable consonant runs (ndsCmptg), phonetic spellings (hilite, xqt, b4), or a misreading (BEND for end of B).
- [Boolean names imply true/false and are stated positively](naming/boolean-variable-names.md) — A boolean named for a thing or dimension (status, state, sourceFile, mode) where true has no clear meaning; a vague success/ok where one specific outcome is meant; or a negated name (notFound, notDone) that ends up under another negation.
- [Name builders with nouns, manipulators with verbs](naming/builder-and-manipulator-names.md) — A method that returns a value is named with a verb (load, read, add, get, cook...), a void method is named with a noun, or a boolean query is named isX/exists; rename to a noun, a verb or an adjective.
- [Computed-value qualifiers go at the end of the name; Count and Index instead of Num](naming/computed-value-qualifier-at-end.md) — One module puts a qualifier in both orders across different quantities (totalRevenue beside expenseTotal, averageExpense beside revenueAverage); a count or position named with Num (numCustomers, customerNum); opposites paired unconventionally (begin/last, first/end).
- [A constant is named for what it stands for, not for its value](naming/constant-names-abstract-not-value.md) — A named constant whose name spells its value (FIVE, TWELVE, TEN_PERCENT, HEX_80) or a well-known quantity (BAKERS_DOZEN) rather than its role, so a change of value would make the name lie.
- [Follow the local naming culture](naming/follow-local-naming-culture.md) — A conventional short name other than a loop index is bound against its convention, such as an error name (err) holding a count or s holding a number.
- [Loop indexes get descriptive names once the loop is long, nested, or the index outlives it](naming/loop-index-names.md) — i, j, k in nested loops or loop bodies longer than a few lines (score[i][j], transaction[j][i][k]); an inner loop reusing an index name an enclosing loop already uses (index cross-talk); a counter read after the loop under a single-letter name; or i/j/k used for anything other than a simple loop index.
- [A name must not mean something else, or nothing at all](naming/misleading-or-arbitrary-names.md) — A name that already means something different (FALSE as an abbreviation, a well-known constant or a language or standard-library name reused for another thing) or that has no relation to what it holds (margaret, pookie, fred, a pet name).
- [Name a thing by its role](naming/name-by-role.md) — A method name states the arithmetic or the mechanism rather than the purpose, a variable carries a generic label, or a primitive parameter leaves its unit unreadable.
- [Name a class for what its objects are](naming/name-classes-for-what-they-are.md) — A class name ends in -er or -or (Manager, Handler, Helper, Validator, Formatter, Sorter), in -able, or in Util/Utils, and names a job done to data rather than the thing its objects encapsulate.
