- [A variable's name fully and accurately describes what it represents](naming/name-describes-what-the-variable-represents.md) — A variable name that is a real word but does not say which quantity it holds: too general for its value (date for today's date, current, total among several totals, data, value) or naming the computer mechanics instead of the problem quantity (inputRec, calcVal).
- [Name an exception after the problem, not after the thrower](naming/name-exceptions-after-the-problem-not-the-thrower.md) — A thrown exception class is named for the component, class or layer that throws it (PersistenceSubsystemException, OrderServiceError) rather than for the cause, so its name says who failed and not why; name each thrown type for the cause (DbUnavailable, ProductNotFound).
- [Name length matches the variable's scope and how often it is used](naming/name-length-matches-scope.md) — One-to-three-letter names (n, ns, lpp) on variables that live past a few lines, are fields or globals, or are rarely referenced; or the opposite, sentence-long names with articles and prepositions that drown statement structure.
- [A name reads at the call site](naming/name-reads-at-the-call-site.md) — A function name repeats its module's name when called with the qualifier, as in Fib.fib(n), so the call stutters and says nothing more.
- [Name every literal except 0 and 1](naming/named-constants-over-literals.md) — A bare number, character or string literal in logic or a loop bound (99, 12, 0x1B, 'Gigamatic'), or one value written as a named constant in one place and as the literal (or literal±1) in another.
- [Names in one scope differ by more than one character](naming/names-differ-by-more-than-a-character.md) — Two names in the same code for different things differ by a single inner letter, a transposed, doubled or dropped letter, only by case, by a look-alike character (1/l/I, 0/O, 2/Z, 5/S, 6/G) or only by sound (clientRecs/clientReps, shiftrn/shiftrm, SYSTSTS/SYSSTSTS, frd/FRD/Frd, wrap/rap).
- [Naming conventions, what they buy and what they encode](naming/naming-conventions.md) — Concept: what a naming convention buys and must distinguish; the one sign kept here is identifiers mixing natural languages or spelling dialects (color/colour) in one codebase; two names for one quantity is one-name-per-concept, loose related data group-related-data-into-a-structure.
- [Digits in names stand in for a collection or a missing distinction](naming/numbered-names.md) — Sibling variables told apart only by a trailing digit (file1, file2, total1, total2, x1, x2) instead of a collection or names that say how they differ.
- [One name per concept, one concept per name](naming/one-name-per-concept.md) — Two identifiers for one thing (client and customer on the same type) with no difference of role between them, sibling operations using different verbs for one action, or one identifier meaning two things, with no glossary settling which is meant.
- [Name range bounds as first, last, lim, min or max, not as end](naming/range-bound-names.md) — A loop or range bound held in a variable named end, top, upper, bound or n, where the reader cannot tell whether it is inclusive or exclusive, or whether it belongs to the array or to the current pass, and it is compared with < at one site and <= at another.
- [Rename extracted code for its new role](naming/rename-extracted-code-for-clarity.md) — A freshly extracted function still carries the caller's names for its locals and parameters (thisAmount, perf), a function name too general for what it does (format for a function used only to format US-dollar amounts), or a placeholder left from a name collision (appleSauce).
- [Rename when meaning drifts](naming/rename-when-meaning-drifts.md) — A name no longer matches the body, such as a get function that writes a file, or a comment has to explain what the name really does.
- [Name a routine for everything it does](naming/routine-names.md) — A routine name built on a vague verb (Handle, Process, Perform, DealWith, Do), told apart from its siblings only by a number (OutputUser1, Part2), omitting an output or side effect the body has, or repeating the receiver in an object method (document.PrintDocument).
- [Self-describing field names](naming/self-describing-field-names.md) — A stored or wire-format key is a position or sequence number such as field10, f_19 or col3, so its value means nothing without the code that decodes it.
- [A local variable should not shadow a field](naming/shadowed-field-names.md) — A local variable declared in a method with the same name as a field of its class, so a bare name means the local and the field is reached only through this.count; or one method writing both count and this.count.
- [No two names with nearly the same meaning in one fragment](naming/similar-meaning-names.md) — One fragment holds two names for different values whose words mean nearly the same thing (input/inputValue, fileNumber/fileIndex, count/total for two counts), so swapping them compiles and is wrong.
- [Name a status variable for the state it records, not "flag"](naming/status-variable-not-flag.md) — A variable whose name is or contains 'flag' (flag, statusFlag, printFlag), especially when it is set or tested against bare numbers like 16 or 0x80.
- [Name an ADT independently of its storage](naming/storage-independent-names.md) — A class or accessor is named after where its data lives (`RateFile.Read()`, `customerDb`, `cacheMap`) rather than what the data is; the name breaks when the storage changes.
- [A "temporary" variable is named for its real role](naming/temporary-variable-names.md) — A variable named temp, tmp, t, x, val, res, result2 or aux holding a single intermediate value that has a nameable meaning (a discriminant root, a subtotal, a price before tax).
- [Variable name more specific than its type name](naming/type-name-vs-variable-name.md) — A variable or parameter named after its type alone (widget: Widget, account: Account, aCustomer: Customer, list: List), so it says what kind of thing it holds but not which one or what for.

## Objects

- [Abstract data type](objects/abstract-data-type.md) — Data plus the operations on it, named in problem terms; the idea a class is supposed to implement, and the test for a class that is only a container of loosely related data and methods.
- [Abstract Factory for families of related objects](objects/abstract-factory.md) — Several creation sites each switch on the same discriminator (vendor, platform, theme) to pick the concrete class of a different member of one family (cash drawer, coin dispenser), so members of different families can be mixed and a new family means editing every switch; let one concrete factory per family create them all behind one factory interface.
- [Abstract, intent-revealing interface](objects/abstract-intent-revealing-interface.md) — Two or more call sites drive one object through the same fixed sequence of its low-level public calls (go, turnRight, turnLeft, stop; open, seek, read, close) to reach one outcome, instead of one call naming the caller's goal (takeTo(airport)).
- [Abstraction and encapsulation](objects/abstraction.md) — Abstraction lets a reader work with a routine, class or package interface while ignoring irrelevant detail; encapsulation forbids seeing past it. An interface that makes a caller handle parts at the wrong level of detail lacks the first.
- [Multiple ADT instances without classes](objects/adt-instances-without-classes.md) — Procedural module exposes `SetCurrentX(id)` and then operations that act on a hidden 'current' instance; choose between passing an id, passing the data record, or implicit current state.
- [Aggregation versus association](objects/aggregation-vs-association.md) — Concept: telling a part a class owns (aggregation: made inside or handed over once, not handed out, ends with the whole) from a collaborator it only uses (association: passed in, shared, outlives the link); the finding is code whose creation, exposure or lifetime handling contradicts the relation chosen.
- [Alternative classes with different interfaces](objects/alternative-classes-with-different-interfaces.md) — Two classes that do the same job, used where one could stand in for the other, expose that job under different method names or parameter orders (sendMail(to, body) beside deliver(body, number)), so callers must know which one they hold.
- [Avoid type introspection and casting](objects/avoid-introspection-and-casting.md) — `instanceof` / type checks or casts on a parameter make a method behave differently per runtime type, hiding a dependency on a second type that the signature does not show.
- [Base class with one subclass](objects/base-class-with-one-subclass.md) — An abstract or base class that has exactly one derived class in the codebase and no test double deriving from it.
- [Choose an alternative to inheritance](objects/choose-an-alternative-to-inheritance.md) — An extends clause to be classified: is the subclass passed where the parent is expected, does it call the parent's methods, or do sibling classes carry the same code?
- [A class interface presents one coherent abstraction](objects/class-interface-coherent-abstraction.md) — A class's public methods serve unrelated purposes (command stack + report printing + global data init), or groups of methods each touch a disjoint half of the fields, or validators of another concept's values have been bolted onto a domain class.
- [Class with only data or only behaviour](objects/class-with-only-data-or-only-behaviour.md) — A class with no fields whose name is an action, created only to call one method on another object's data (new DatabaseInitialization().run(db)); or a field-less class whose methods all take the same one record and work only on its fields, while that record has only fields and accessors (Cab and CabService).
- [Collapse hierarchy](objects/collapse-hierarchy.md) — A subclass (or its parent) left with an empty body, or with only a constructor that passes its arguments to super, after features were pulled up or pushed down: merge the two classes into one.
- [Combine Functions into Class](objects/combine-functions-into-class.md) — Several free functions or client fragments take the same bare record as their main input and compute derived values from it (base charge, taxable charge), the same formula is repeated or extracted far from the data, and the record is updated somewhere after the values are derived: make the record a class whose methods compute the values on demand.
- [Composable decorators](objects/composable-decorators.md) — Small objects that each wrap one other object and add one behaviour, nested into a single expression (new Sorted(new Unique(new Capitalized(...)))) instead of a long method doing all steps in sequence.
- [Composite: the group implements the part's interface](objects/composite-same-interface-as-part.md) — A client holds either one item or a list of the same type (one pricing strategy or several, a command or a macro) and branches on which it has, or several client methods loop over the same collection and fold its results by the same rule; make the group implement the same interface as the single item.
- [Constructors hold no code](objects/constructors-without-code.md) — A constructor body parses, converts, validates, calls methods on its arguments or does I/O, instead of only assigning arguments, raw, or wrapped in objects by a secondary constructor, to fields.
- [Containment or inheritance](objects/containment-or-inheritance.md) — Several classes declare the same group of fields with no shared object holding them; a class extends one of its own parts, so the sentence 'every X is a Y' is false (Car extends Engine, Television extends Tuner); also the decision test (share data, behaviour or both; who defines the interface) that an extends clause raised elsewhere is judged by.
- [Contract via abstract methods](objects/contract-via-abstract-methods.md) — Concept: Weisfeld's 'contract' is a method left unimplemented in an abstract class or interface, so the compiler rejects a concrete subclass that does not supply it; it fixes signatures only and is not Design by Contract.
- [Controller: the class that receives system operations coordinates, it does not do the work](objects/controller.md) — The class that receives the program's incoming requests or system operations computes the results itself (loops and arithmetic over domain data, line items and totals in its own fields) instead of delegating, or one such class takes every operation of many unrelated use cases; split per use case or delegate. A UI handler computing business results is logic-testable-without-ui.
- [Creator: the class that contains, records or initializes A creates A](objects/creator.md) — A class runs `new A(...)` and hands the result straight to another object that stores it, using A for nothing else, so it depends on A only to build it; the part belongs to the object that contains, records or holds the initializing data for it.
- [Declarative style in objects](objects/declarative-style.md) — Objects that declare what a value is (new Between(5, 9, 13)) rather than computing it at the call (Math.between(5, 9, 13)): evaluation on demand, substitution through constructors, and lines bound into one expression so they cannot be reordered by mistake.
- [Deep inheritance hierarchy](objects/deep-inheritance-hierarchy.md) — An inheritance chain more than three of the project's own levels below the root, or a base class with more than about nine subclasses in all, so understanding a call at the leaf means reading several ancestors.
- [Delegate to services](objects/delegate-to-services.md) — A class extending a framework, persistence or project base class, exposing that class's whole API to its callers while it and they use only a few of its methods (inherited by accident, not is-a); save or query methods on a domain class where the project's convention keeps persistence out of domain classes.
- [Describe variants in data, not subclasses](objects/describe-variants-in-data-not-subclasses.md) — N methods or N subclasses, one per record/message type, each a straight-line sequence of the same read/print/convert steps over a different field list, plus an if/factory chain on the type id: replace with one description table per type and one interpreter.
- [Do not reuse the names of non-overridable base methods](objects/do-not-reuse-names-of-non-overridable-methods.md) — A subclass declares a method with the same name as a private or non-overridable method of its base, so a reader takes it for a polymorphic override.
- [Elegant Objects (Bugayenko)](objects/elegant-objects.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: a deliberately radical book on objects (nouns for class names, constructors without code, small immutable objects, no static methods, getters or NULL, recovery only at entry points, classes final or abstract) that disagrees with common practice and with The Pragmatic Programmer in places.
- [Encapsulate a collection field](objects/encapsulate-collection.md) — A getter returns the object's own mutable collection field (return this.items), or a setter stores the caller's list as is, so clients add, remove or sort the member list without the owning class seeing it.
- [Extract superclass](objects/extract-superclass.md) — Two classes with no common parent each declare the same field (name, id) and a method with the same body over a corresponding value (annualCost = monthlyCost * 12 beside totalAnnualCost = totalMonthlyCost * 12), often under different names; a repeated field group alone, with no shared method, is containment-or-inheritance.
- [Factory function over a constructor](objects/factory-function-over-constructor.md) — Call sites outside any factory pass a constructor a literal type code (new Employee(name, 'E')), or replace or wrap the object right after constructing it depending on arguments or environment (if remote: s = Proxy(s)); wrap creation in a named factory function.
- [Factory object for complex or variable creation](objects/factory-object-for-creation.md) — A domain or business class chooses which concrete class to instantiate (branching on configuration, vendor or type code) or carries many lines of construction logic inside a method whose job is something else; move the choice and the construction into a separate factory object that returns the interface.
- [Fewer than five public methods](objects/fewer-than-five-public-methods.md) — A class exposing five or more public or protected methods (constructors and private methods not counted) is too large: check whether its fields split into groups used by disjoint sets of methods, and split it along that line.
- [Be either final or abstract](objects/final-or-abstract.md) — A subclass overrides a method that its parent, concrete or abstract, implements and does not mark final, typically one the parent's other methods call, so the parent's method changes behaviour without its code changing; also a class with a subclass, overridable methods its own methods call, and no documented inheritance policy.
- [God class](objects/god-class.md) — A class that reads and writes the data of several other classes through their getters and setters and decides for them, while those classes hold data and little behaviour.
- [Hide the delegate or remove the middle man](objects/hide-delegate-or-remove-middle-man.md) — A class whose public methods are mostly one-line forwards to the same field, in the domain's own vocabulary, adding nothing (middle man); also a client reaching two steps through B's accessor to call C (a.b().c()), and the decision whether B should hide C or step aside.
- [Information Expert: give a responsibility to the class that has the information](objects/information-expert.md) — A method in class X computes a derived value (total, subtotal, status) only from data class Y holds, reading it out through getters and writing nothing back, when Y could compute it from its own state; a read followed by a write back into Y is tell-dont-ask.
- [Inheritance tax](objects/inheritance-tax.md) — A subclass of a concrete class that reads the parent's fields, or a call site calling, through the subclass, a method declared only in the parent.
- [Inheritance weakens encapsulation](objects/inheritance-weakens-encapsulation.md) — Concept: a subclass inherits its parent's implementation, so a change inside a concrete parent method is not hidden from the subclass and ripples down the hierarchy (Cabbie.giveDirections reaching PartTimeCabbie), while a class that only calls the parent's public interface is insulated from it.
- [Interface and implementation](objects/interface-and-implementation.md) — Concept: a class's interface is everything a caller can depend on (public signatures, return values and observable behaviour); everything else is implementation. A change a caller can observe is an interface change even when no signature moved, and a public signature naming a storage format or vendor type makes every implementation change an interface change.
- [Introduce Special Case (Null Object)](objects/introduce-special-case.md) — Several clients compare one field to the same sentinel value ("unknown", null, an empty marker) and most give it the same answer (the same placeholder name, default plan or zero), or skip a write when it holds: move that answer into one special-case object with the normal interface.
- [Iterator: traverse without exposing the collection's structure](objects/iterator.md) — A function only loops over its argument yet declares it as a concrete collection class (or an array plus an index or length); a class returns its internal collection field so callers can loop over it; or a loop outside a collection's class walks its storage (backing-array indexes, node links).
- [Keep objects small](objects/keep-objects-small.md) — A class stores more than four fields (Elegant Objects conventions) or more than about seven (elsewhere, after Code Complete), its constructor takes more than five parameters, fields share a prefix that names a missing child object (cardNumber, cardExpiry on a payment, often with logic interpreting them), or a Builder exists to assemble it.
- [Applying UML and Patterns (Larman), GRASP and GoF chapters](objects/larman-applying-uml-and-patterns.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: the GRASP and GoF chapters of Larman's textbook (17, 18, 25, 26, 35), which teach assigning responsibilities to objects by nine named principles (Expert, Creator, Controller, Low Coupling, High Cohesion, Polymorphism, Pure Fabrication, Indirection, Protected Variations) and then read the GoF patterns as their specializations, on the NextGen POS and Monopoly case studies.
- [Liskov substitution principle](objects/liskov-substitution-principle.md) — A subclass method keeps the base method's name and signature but changes what the result means (sign, unit, direction), or throws 'not supported', so callers holding the base type branch on the subtype or correct the result.
- [The lock belongs to the resource](objects/lock-belongs-to-the-resource.md) — Callers acquire and release a lock around access to an object, the lock sits beside the data rather than inside it, or the same lock/unlock pair repeats at several call sites: one forgotten caller breaks the protection.
- [Minimise the accessibility of classes and members](objects/minimize-member-accessibility.md) — A method is public though it does not fit the class's abstraction: made public 'because it only uses public methods', added to the interface to make one particular client's code easier to write, or a step of a public operation (turnRight under giveDestination) declared public though only the class's own methods call it.
- [Mixed abstraction levels in a class interface](objects/mixed-abstraction-levels-in-interface.md) — A class's public methods mix domain-level operations with operations of the container or library it is built on (`AddEmployee` beside `FirstItem`, `NextItemInList`), often because it inherits from the container or a wrapper re-exposes the whole wrapped API.
- [Share functionality with mixins](objects/mixins-share-functionality.md) — The same finder or helper methods repeated across sibling classes; one class holding every validation, with flags choosing which run in which situation.
- [Multiple inheritance only for mixins](objects/multiple-inheritance-only-for-mixins.md) — A class inherits implementation from two or more parents that are not small independent mixins (Displayable, Persistent, Sortable), or from mixins that depend on each other.
- [No getters and setters](objects/no-getters-and-setters.md) — A class whose public surface is getX()/setX(v) pairs over its private fields, with no method that works with those fields, is a data structure dressed as an object.
- [Share functionality, not data: no public constants](objects/no-public-constants.md) — A public static constant, an enum value or a Constants holder class is read by unrelated classes that each wrap it in their own code, or is passed into a general class to select its behaviour (`.method(HttpMethods.POST)`); replace it with a small class that owns that behaviour.
- [No singletons](objects/no-singletons.md) — A class declares a static INSTANCE of its own type, a non-public constructor and a static getInstance() (or setInstance() for tests): it is a global variable; create the object once where the application is assembled and pass it through constructors.
- [No static methods](objects/no-static-methods.md) — Behaviour exposed as static methods or a utility class (private constructor, only static members, e.g. XUtils.doThing(x)) cannot be substituted or composed; replace it with an object that takes its inputs in the constructor, and wrap unavoidable library statics in one adapter class.
- [Null field hides another class](objects/null-field-hides-another-class.md) — A field initialised to null and filled by a later setter, or a group of fields set only in one mode, with code branching on `field != null` to decide what kind of object this is (Fowler's temporary field).
- [Object as representative, not conduit](objects/object-as-representative.md) — A class whose objects only move data through themselves: its methods are procedures over fields that callers pass in or read out. An object should stand for the data it encapsulates and decide for itself how to answer requests.
- [Define how a class compares, instead of trusting the default](objects/object-equality.md) — A value-like class (meaning lies wholly in its fields) defines no equality while code compares instances with == or uses them in sets or as keys; an equality that compares sub-objects by reference where their contents matter; or an equality with no matching hash.
- [The Object-Oriented Thought Process (Weisfeld)](objects/object-oriented-thought-process.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: an introductory book on thinking in objects before learning a language (interface against implementation, a minimal public interface, private attributes, constructors that leave a stable state, composition against inheritance, abstract classes and interfaces as contracts), followed by chapters on data exchange, persistence, web clients and three design patterns.
- [Object persistence](objects/object-persistence.md) — Concept: what saving an object stores is its state (attribute values), not its behaviour or its invariants; a composite saved without its parts comes back incomplete, and a native serialized form ties every reader to the class definition and its private fields, while a mapped portable form is a contract declared apart from them.
- [Make one constructor primary](objects/one-primary-constructor.md) — Two or more constructors of one class each assign the object's fields, so a check or conversion added to one of them is missing from the others.
- [An overloaded operator keeps the meaning readers expect](objects/operator-overloading-meaning.md) — An operator overload whose body departs from what the symbol means for values of that kind: + that removes or subtracts, an operator that mutates its operand where the built-in one returns a new value, or an arithmetic overload that combines mismatched units without a check.
- [Override that does nothing](objects/override-that-does-nothing.md) — A subclass overrides an inherited method with an empty body (or one that only returns/ignores) because this kind of object lacks the ability (ScratchlessCat.scratch, a penguin's fly); class names start to stack negations such as ScratchlessTaillessCat. Seen from the base: a behaviour only some subclasses have, placed in the parent.
- [Design patterns as specializations of GRASP principles](objects/patterns-as-specializations-of-grasp.md) — Concept: each GoF pattern pays for an indirection with protection from one named variation (Adapter from varying interfaces, Strategy from changing algorithms, Observer from the number and class of listeners); judging a pattern in code means asking whether that variation is present.
- [Polymorphism or type switch](objects/polymorphism-or-type-switch.md) — A switch over an object's type code that calls a type-specific method or routine in each arm (drawCircle, drawSquare; processDeposit(t), processWithdrawal(t)) on the same object or data, the same type code switched on in several routines, one special case (zone == china and has china history) tested in several functions of one calculation, or two hierarchies whose subclasses mirror each other; distinguish it from a switch dispatching genuinely different commands, and from the one creation switch in a factory.
- [Prefer interfaces for polymorphism](objects/prefer-interfaces-for-polymorphism.md) — A base class with no shared behaviour, there only so unrelated classes fit one collection; a class needing a second parent; a hierarchy level no code is typed by.
- [Make base class data private, not protected](objects/private-data-not-protected.md) — An abstract base class declares protected fields that subclasses read or assign directly; with a concrete parent the same shape is inheritance-tax.
- [Provide operations with their opposites](objects/provide-opposite-operations.md) — A public operation has no counterpart where the domain implies one: `add` without `remove`, `turnOn` without `turnOff`, `enable` without `disable`, `open` without `close`.
- [Proxy: control access through a surrogate that has the subject's interface](objects/proxy.md) — Two or more call sites of one service repeat the same wrapper around the call (try the remote and fall back to a local copy, check a cache, check a permission), or a client holds a remote and a local implementation of one service and picks between them; move that logic into a proxy that implements the service's interface and holds the real subject.
- [Every public method implements an interface](objects/public-methods-implement-interfaces.md) — Under the Elegant Objects convention a public method that overrides no interface method; anywhere, a field or parameter typed by a concrete project class whose behaviour a caller could need to replace (not a string, date or collection); route it through an interface.
- [Pull Up Constructor Body](objects/pull-up-constructor-body.md) — Every subclass constructor repeats the same assignments or calls after super() (this.name = name; if isPrivileged() then assignCar()): move them into the superclass constructor through the super call, or into a pulled-up method called at the end when ordering prevents it.
- [Pull Up Method and Pull Up Field](objects/pull-up-method.md) — Two or more sibling subclasses each define a method or field that their superclass does not declare, with the same body or the same use, possibly under different names (annualCost / totalAnnualCost): make the copies identical, then keep one copy on the superclass.
- [Pure Fabrication: when the information expert is the wrong home](objects/pure-fabrication.md) — Deciding whether a responsibility stays with the class that owns the data or moves to a made-up class: move it when it brings in operations unrelated to the concept, a technical interface or a task many classes repeat; own sign: a domain method acts on a group it holds and keeps the computed value only in a local (Player rolls and sums the dice inside takeTurn), so the value cannot be had without repeating the action.
- [Push Down Method and Push Down Field](objects/push-down-method-and-field.md) — A superclass method or field that only one subclass, or a few, read, write or call (a quota field on Employee that only Salesman assigns), or that other subclasses override with an empty body or a throw: move it to those subclasses, provided callers already hold the subclass type.
- [Reasons to create a class](objects/reasons-to-create-a-class.md) — A class that cannot be justified by any of the listed reasons (hiding a detail, isolating complexity or a likely change, a central point of control, grouping parameters passed together) is a candidate to remove.
- [Reference or value for a nested object](objects/reference-or-value.md) — A holder's setter writes a field of a nested object only that holder refers to (this.phone.areaCode = x: make it a value), or every holder constructs its own copy of the same logical record from one id and some code then updates one copy (new Customer(data.customerId) per order: make it a shared reference).
- [Replace Conditional with Polymorphism: the mechanics](objects/replace-conditional-with-polymorphism.md) — Procedure for turning the same switch on a type code (play.type, kind) in several functions into a class hierarchy: host class, move the functions in, factory with the one remaining switch, then move one case at a time into subclass overrides, leaving a throwing tombstone and a default in the superclass.
- [Replace direct data manipulation with an abstract data type](objects/replace-direct-data-manipulation-with-adt.md) — Client code sets fields, flag bits or unit-ambiguous numbers of a shared structure directly (`font.attribute = font.attribute or 0x02`, `font.size = 16`) in several places, or digs into a widely used map or nested record on both sides of an assignment (`customers[id].usages[y][m] = v`), instead of calling named operations.
- [Replace subclass with delegate](objects/replace-subclass-with-delegate.md) — Subclasses that cover one axis of variation while a second axis is needed (combination subclasses such as YoungWealthy), or code that rebuilds an object as another subclass to change its kind at run time (copying fields into a new PremiumX and re-pointing references); move the varying behaviour into a delegate held by a field.
- [Replace superclass with delegate](objects/replace-superclass-with-delegate.md) — A subclass that extends a class describing a kind of thing while it represents one physical instance or copy of that kind (PhysicalCar extends CarModel, Scroll extends CatalogItem), so the kind's data is copied into every instance: the type-instance homonym. Hold the kind in a field, shared by reference, and forward to it instead.
- [Replace Type Code with Subclasses](objects/replace-type-code-with-subclasses.md) — A class with a type-code field (enum, string, number) that also carries fields or methods meaningful only for some codes (a quota only salesmen have, guarded by if type == "salesman"), or a constructor validating the code against a list; replace the code with subclasses, of the class itself or, if the type changes at run time or the class is already subclassed, of a separate type object.
- [Responsibility-driven design](objects/responsibility-driven-design.md) — Concept: deciding which class a method belongs to by first naming the responsibility it carries out (a doing or a knowing) and then giving that responsibility to a class; a method is judged by the responsibility it fulfils, not by its name; a class named after a human role is judged by whose data its steps use, not by what the person does. The frame under the GRASP pages.
- [Semantic violations of encapsulation](objects/semantic-encapsulation-violation.md) — Caller code skips a documented call, borrows another class's constant, or keeps a reference because it knows what the other class does inside (skips `connect()` since `retrieve()` connects anyway), or a class demands an undocumented behaviour from its clients.
- [Make interfaces programmatic rather than semantic](objects/semantic-interface-to-programmatic.md) — A precondition on a value or state of an interface lives only in a comment ('x must be initialised first', 'pass a non-empty list'), or a class has a public initialize() its other methods need first, with no type, constructor or assertion enforcing it.
- [Put identical behavior in the superclass and make only the varying step polymorphic](objects/shared-behavior-in-superclass-varying-step-polymorphic.md) — Sibling subclasses of one project superclass override the same method with bodies that match line for line except one expression or call; implement the method once in the superclass and make only that step a polymorphic operation.
- [Keep interfaces small; put derived convenience methods in a smart class](objects/small-interface-with-smart-class.md) — An interface declares a method that every implementation can compute from another method of the same interface (an overload filling a default argument, a shortcut for a fixed value), so each implementer must rewrite the same convenience logic.
- [Strategy for varying algorithms or policies](objects/strategy-for-varying-algorithms.md) — A method holds an if/switch chain over a policy setting (discount type, pricing rule, scoring mode), each arm computing the same result by a different algorithm with its own parameters stored on the context; give each variant its own class behind one interface held by the context.
- [Subclass that differs only in data](objects/subclass-that-differs-only-in-data.md) — A derived class that overrides nothing but constants or fixed return values (Male and Female overriding genderCode), often tested by clients with instanceof or chosen by a loader's switch on a data code, or a class constructed at exactly one site, where an object of an existing class with different field values would do.
- [Tell, don't ask](objects/tell-dont-ask.md) — Outside code reads an object's fields or getters, decides, then writes back through setters to that same object.
- [Uniform access](objects/uniform-access.md) — Code outside a class reads or writes an object's fields directly (public fields, or fields reached past the object's methods), so turning a stored value into a computed one would change every call site and the class cannot know or control the change.

## Structure

- [Access routines at the level of the problem domain](structure/access-routines-at-domain-level.md) — Callers mix direct access to a shared structure (node = node.next, queue[front], stack.array[stack.top], count = count - 1) with access routines like PushStack() on the same data, or the routines are named in the implementation's terms, so the code speaks in the implementation's terms and the routines' checks are skipped at the direct sites.
- [Architecture prototype questions](structure/architecture-prototype-questions.md) — A module needs data it cannot reach, or cannot reach when it needs it: for each datum a module reads, ask who produces it and at what point in the run.
- [Blackboard](structure/blackboard.md) — A coordinator with branches over which inputs have arrived so far, such as `if a and b and not c`, holding the handling of every input and rule in one function: facts arrive in any order and the sequence is hard-coded anyway.
- [Business rules are metadata](structure/business-rules-are-metadata.md) — The same condition naming concrete roles, departments or limits repeats at two or more sites: the policy is hard-coded instead of held as data read by one mechanism.
- [Circular dependency](structure/circular-dependency.md) — A method of class A calls class B and a method of B calls back into A's concrete type, so neither can be built or tested without the other.
- [Class data versus global data](structure/class-data-versus-global-data.md) — Fields shared by dozens of methods of one large class behave like global data; fields of a small class whose few methods all know each other do not.
- [Cohesion](structure/cohesion.md) — How closely all routines of a class, or all parts of a routine, serve one central purpose; low cohesion shows as members a reader cannot relate to the class's name, as one class serving several unrelated functional areas, or as one area carried alone by a class with hundreds of methods. Larman's High Cohesion grades the degrees and names when lower cohesion is accepted.
- [Keep configuration behind a thin API](structure/configuration-behind-a-thin-api.md) — A global config map read at many call sites; raw key paths, environment variable names or file format details spread outside one module.
- [Coupling hidden in language features](structure/coupling-hidden-in-language-features.md) — Multiple inheritance, exceptions, operator overloading, overridden parent methods and shared data formats add coupling that is not visible at the call site.
- [Coupling](structure/coupling.md) — Concept: a class or routine tied to another so they change together; graded by size (parameter count, public methods), visibility (parameter against hidden global) and flexibility (how easily a new caller can use it); transitive; module-to-module dependencies are taken from the architecture.
- [Design heuristics for construction](structure/design-heuristics.md) — Checklist to run while designing a class, and against an existing one: find the objects, form consistent abstractions, hide secrets (one sentence names the class's secret), isolate likely change, keep coupling loose; for review, decomposition into classes and methods, minimal interaction, complete but minimal, standard techniques.
- [Divergent change and shotgun surgery](structure/divergent-change-vs-shotgun-surgery.md) — Concept: two opposite failures of 'one change, one place' after Fowler: one class serving two unrelated concerns (tax rules beside line formatting), or one concern spread as small fragments across many classes; names the code-visible shapes, routes them to their owners, and holds Fowler's repairs for each.
- [Do not rely on unguaranteed context](structure/do-not-rely-on-unguaranteed-context.md) — A utility module reads an environment variable, the current directory, a UI handle or locale directly, or makes a network call with no timeout or failure path.
- [Encapsulate Variable: the mechanics](structure/encapsulate-variable.md) — Procedure for mutable data whose scope is wider than one function (a module-level variable, a public field): route every read and write through a getter and setter, test after each replaced reference, then restrict the variable's visibility; make the getter return a copy where callers must not change the shared value. Not needed for immutable data or one function's temps.
- [Event-driven code](structure/event-driven-code.md) — Reacting code with no chosen strategy, so that handlers tangle together: map the shape of the problem to a state machine, observer, publish-subscribe or an event stream.
- [Event stream](structure/event-stream.md) — Events treated as a collection that grows as they arrive, so they can be filtered, merged and zipped; the alternative is hand-kept timers, counters and buffers correlating asynchronous callbacks.
- [Facade: one entry point to a group of classes](structure/facade-single-entry-point.md) — Client classes import and call several classes of one group of the project's own code (a loader, an evaluator, a cache) to perform one service, each client repeating the same call sequence, so replacing the group means editing every client; give the group one front object and make the rest private.
- [Find what can run concurrently](structure/find-what-can-run-concurrently.md) — Sequential statements or awaits in one function, some waiting on a database, a service or a user, some doing independent heavy computation: separate real dependencies from written order, then decide per step between concurrency, parallelism or leaving it sequential.
- [Framework intrusion](structure/framework-intrusion.md) — Application code must create or reach objects in a way a library dictates, or business functions open and commit transactions themselves.
- [Global data](structure/global-data.md) — A function's body reaches a non-constant module-level name, static field, singleton accessor or `Config.x`, or calls a database, file system or service directly, or an instance method or static setter assigns a static field that every instance reads, so its dependencies are hidden from the signature and its test must first build a global environment; also a global passed as an argument to a routine that writes it by name (aliasing), intermediate results stored in a global, or one oversized context object passed to every routine.
- [Hide a design decision behind one access point](structure/hide-secrets-behind-one-access-point.md) — A representation decision leaks into code that uses the value: a primitive type standing for a domain value is declared and compared with < across modules (int id, id1 < id2), so a change of its representation touches every declaration.
- [High-level code in problem terms](structure/high-level-code-in-problem-terms.md) — A routine at the top of a call chain (entry point, use case, handler) that names file modes, record layouts, byte offsets, stack or queue operations, or a one-letter index for a domain thing, often with a comment translating that variable into the domain.
- [Information hiding](structure/information-hiding.md) — Concept: each class, routine or package is defined by the design decision (secret) it keeps from the rest; its absence shows as a representation detail (how a value is made, its type, a size, a file format) visible where the value is used.
- [Wrap legacy and platform calls in one class](structure/isolate-volatile-dependencies-behind-a-layer.md) — Calls into the program's own poor-quality legacy code or a non-portable platform API, with their quirks (error codes, sentinel values, odd names) and the workarounds for them, appear at several call sites instead of being translated once inside one wrapper class.
- [Limit fan-out](structure/limit-fan-out.md) — A routine calls more than about seven distinct modules, classes or services, or a class's method bodies reach more than about seven collaborator types beyond the types of its fields.
- [Logic testable without the UI](structure/logic-testable-without-ui.md) — A test of a calculation or decision has to open a form and simulate clicks, an event handler computes and branches while reading widget fields directly, one function both computes a business result and builds its output, domain code calls a dialog to report to the user, or other code reaches the logic through a hidden form or a parallel copy of it.
- [Low Coupling: choose the placement that adds no dependency on unstable elements](structure/low-coupling.md) — Of two workable placements for one responsibility, the chosen one adds a field, parameter, local, return type, superclass or implemented interface naming a class the other placement would not need (a reference kept only for one method); or an interface or adapter stands in front of a stable, pervasive dependency with no named reason to vary (a one-occupant pattern role is do-not-force-a-design-pattern, any other single-implementation layer is know-when-to-stop where a change adds it and minimal-but-complete-functionality in code as it stands).
- [Name friction exposes needless coupling](structure/name-friction-exposes-coupling.md) — A local bound to a whole object from a lookup, read for one field and dropped, in a module that uses the object's type nowhere else: the code depends on more than it needs, so ask for the value itself.
- [Near-decomposability: fewer links between parts than within them](structure/near-decomposability.md) — Concept: Simon's near-decomposability as Weisfeld uses it to justify composition, fewer links between parts than within them; parts of a class that read each other's fields or call each other back and forth have their boundary in the wrong place, and the coupling and cohesion rules apply it.
- [`new` only in secondary constructors](structure/new-only-in-secondary-constructors.md) — `new Collaborator()` inside a method body or the primary constructor hard-codes a dependency the caller cannot replace (e.g. a network call in every unit test).
- [Observer: the publisher knows its subscribers only by interface](structure/observer-publisher-knows-only-interface.md) — A model or domain class holds a field typed as a concrete window, mailer or other reacting class and calls it after changing state, so each new reaction means editing the publisher; make it notify registered listeners through an interface it owns.
- [Observer or publish-subscribe](structure/observer-vs-publish-subscribe.md) — A method doing other work loops over callbacks inline and a callback in view blocks (I/O, network, a lock) or raises a failure that work does not handle; or code publishes on a channel and its next lines depend on what a subscriber did.
- [Hold text in one internal format; convert at input and output](structure/one-internal-string-format.md) — Encoding or string-type conversions (to/from bytes, wide strings, legacy charsets) scattered through core logic, one value passed through core functions sometimes as bytes and sometimes as text, or user-visible strings written as literals in code that already looks up other messages by key.
- [Tests for orthogonality](structure/orthogonality-tests.md) — Checks to run on code: modules touched by one requirement, imports a unit test needs, spread of a bug fix, files per fix in history, and what a library demands of your objects.
- [Orthogonality](structure/orthogonality.md) — One change forces edits in unrelated modules, or a fix here breaks something elsewhere: components are not independent.
- [Process values, not their source](structure/process-values-not-their-source.md) — A class doing one computation that takes a file name or reads input itself: pass it the values, so the source can change without touching it.
- [Program into the language, not in it](structure/program-into-the-language.md) — Concept: Gries's distinction between letting the language's constructs and defaults set the design (in) and deciding the design first, then expressing it with the language plus conventions and helpers (into); its signs live on the pages it points to: a hidden form or parallel copy of UI logic, ad-hoc surfaces or checks, a global or goto used because the language allows it.
- [Protected Variations](structure/protected-variations.md) — Concept: find the points of predicted variation or instability and put a stable interface around them; information hiding, the open-closed principle, polymorphism, indirection and the Law of Demeter are forms of it; at a speculative evolution point protection can cost more than reworking a simple design, and this wiki routes that call to replaceable-code-over-forecast.
- [Representational duplication](structure/representational-duplication.md) — A hand-written structure mirrors an external schema field by field, or error codes and API shapes are copied by hand where a machine-readable definition exists.
- [Semantic coupling](structure/semantic-coupling.md) — A caller relies on what a callee does inside rather than on its interface: it passes a literal (true/false, an int code, an enum member, a string such as "premium") that selects which branch of the callee runs, or builds an argument only partly because it knows which fields the callee reads.
- [One owner for direct access to stored data](structure/single-owner-of-data-access.md) — The same table name, file path, key prefix or record layout (column order, field offsets) appears in query or parse code in two or more classes or modules that are not its declared owner, instead of behind one class that owns it.
- [Start with the smallest scope](structure/smallest-scope-first.md) — A variable declared wider than its uses: a routine-level local read only inside one loop, a field read and written only within a single method call, a non-public field nothing outside its class (and no subclass) touches.
- [Temporal coupling](structure/temporal-coupling.md) — A comment says 'call X before Y' across objects or where the callee holds no state to check it, a sleep waits for a result, a flag makes callers take turns over work that shares nothing, independent backend calls run one after another, or an object built empty is completed by setters before use: the code depends on order in time and nothing states it.
- [Top-down and bottom-up design](structure/top-down-and-bottom-up-design.md) — Decomposition (general to specific) vs composition (specific to general); decomposition stops when the next level would be easier to code than to decompose, and a solution that still looks slightly tricky needs another level.
- [Train wreck (chained method calls)](structure/train-wreck.md) — An expression walks more than two dotted steps, fields or calls alike, through objects returned by other objects, or does the same through a run of temporaries each derived from the last.

## Testing

- [Adding tests to existing code before refactoring](testing/adding-tests-to-existing-code.md) — Procedure for putting untested code under test before changing it: write the test with a placeholder, copy in what the code actually produces, inject a fault, see the test fail with expected and actual values, revert; then pin outputs, state changes and boundaries in that order.
- [All tests pass, all the time](testing/all-tests-pass-always.md) — A test is switched off instead of fixed: a skip or expected-failure marker with no stated condition, a commented-out body, or an exclusion by name in configuration. One tolerated failure hides the next.
- [Boundary value analysis](testing/boundary-value-analysis.md) — Procedure for a comparison like x < max or x >= limit with no test at max-1, max and max+1, or arithmetic and totals over several inputs with no test of all inputs at their extremes together.
- [Brittle tests](testing/brittle-tests.md) — An assertion compares exact error text, a log timestamp, an absolute screen position or a private field read by reflection, so the test fails after a change that kept every return value and visible effect the same.
- [Code coverage measurement](testing/code-coverage.md) — Concept: testing without a coverage monitor typically exercises only 50-60% of the code; the monitor names untested lines, which call for more tests, but covered lines are not thereby tested.
- [Code inspection](testing/code-inspection.md) — Procedure for reviewing code by reading it against a one-page checklist of known defect types, detecting rather than fixing; catches unclear error messages, misleading comments, hard-coded values and duplication that no test exposes.
- [Data-flow testing](testing/data-flow-testing.md) — Procedure adding tests for every definition-use pair of a variable that branch-based tests miss, e.g. x set in branch A of one if and used in branch B of a later if.
- [Defect-detection techniques are complementary](testing/defect-detection-techniques-are-complementary.md) — Concept: a green suite is taken as proof of a change, but a typical unit or integration test level finds about 30-35% of defects; reading code finds interface defects that tests miss and shows the cause, not just the symptom.
- [Developer testing](testing/developer-testing.md) — Concept: what tests written by the code's own author can and cannot show; a passing suite never proves absence of defects, and authors overrate both their coverage (believed 95%, typically 50-60%) and the breadth of their cases.
- [Equivalence partitioning](testing/equivalence-partitioning.md) — Procedure for when several tests feed inputs from the same class (three salaries all below a threshold) while another class of the same condition has no test: one representative per class, drop the rest.
- [Find bugs once](testing/find-bugs-once.md) — A diff fixes a defect and touches no test, or a comment stands in for a test: a warning about the failure, a note of a manual check, a snippet to paste into a REPL. The same bug can return unnoticed.
- [Build a fresh fixture for each test](testing/fresh-fixture-per-test.md) — A mutable test object built once at suite, class or module scope, or in a run-once hook, and read by several tests; strongest when a test changes it, so results depend on run order.
- [Build an independent checking tool](testing/independent-checking-tool.md) — Use when outputs of a complex calculation are checked by hand, or a failure cannot be placed in the data or in the program: write a separate one-case program that recomputes a result, or a validator for the input data, independent of the main system's code.
- [One verification per test](testing/one-verification-per-test.md) — One test case asserts two or more independent results of the code under test (shortfall, then profit, then the effect of a change), so the first failed assertion stops the test and hides whether the others hold.
- [Prefer fakes shipped with the interface over mocks](testing/prefer-fakes-over-mocks.md) — A test stubs or verifies calls on a collaborator through a mocking framework (when(x).rate(..).thenReturn, verify(x, times(n))), so it fails when the class under test changes how it uses that collaborator while its visible behaviour stays the same.
- [Property-based testing](testing/property-based-testing.md) — A function whose tests are only hand-picked examples while it has a statable contract, invariant or inverse (round trip, length kept, sorted output): state it as a property over generated inputs and pin each falsifying input as a unit test.
- [Regression testing: the same tests every time, automated](testing/regression-testing.md) — A test that failed after a change was deleted, or its expected value edited to match the new output, with no stated reason the old expectation was wrong; regression testing means the same automated tests every time, old ones kept.
- [Sabotage your tests](testing/sabotage-your-tests.md) — Procedure for a test whose ability to fail was never seen: inject the fault it guards against, confirm it goes red for that reason, and strengthen it if it stays green.
- [Self-testing code](testing/self-testing-code.md) — Concept: an automated suite fast enough to run after every small step and sure to fail on a programming error; what refactoring rests on. Without it, only tool-automated safe refactorings remain, or tests inserted at seams first. Its payoff is that a failure points at the last few minutes of change.
- [Smoke test](testing/smoke-test.md) — Concept: a shallow end-to-end run of the whole built system that decides whether a build is fit for deeper testing; a pipeline whose only post-build check is that the build succeeded, or an entry point of the built system that no smoke-test step invokes, gives false confidence.
- [Structured basis testing](testing/structured-basis-testing.md) — Procedure to count the minimum tests a routine needs (1, plus each if/while/for/and/or, plus each case and a missing default) and derive one true and one false case per decision, so every statement runs.
- [Test boundaries and realistic use](testing/test-boundaries-and-realistic-use.md) — Every test of an operation with a direction, order or sign in its arguments uses the same direction, order or sign, so real usage along that axis never runs.
- [Test by risk, not by method](testing/test-by-risk-not-by-method.md) — A suite with tests for accessors that only read or write a field, while a function in the same unit with branches, loops, sorting or side effects on other objects has no test, or only a happy-path one.
- [Tests carry as many defects as the code they test](testing/test-code-is-defect-prone.md) — A test computes its expected value with loops or branches that re-implement the code under test, so a shared mistake passes; tests hold as many defects as the code, so they are built and reviewed like code.
- [Error guessing and classes of bad and good data](testing/test-data-classes.md) — Checklist procedure for test inputs: too little, too much, wrong kind, wrong size and uninitialized data; nominal, minimum normal and maximum normal configurations; compatibility with old data; plus a kept list of past errors.
- [Test-driven development](testing/test-driven-development.md) — A run of new tests exercises one internal representation and none calls the operation the requirement names, or a test only references a class name: the test-first cycle is producing green bars, not progress.
- [Test early, often and automatically](testing/test-early-often-automatically.md) — A test prints a value for a person to compare instead of asserting, needs a hand-run step, or new logic arrives in a diff with no test. A test that exists and is switched off is all-tests-pass-always.
- [Test environment matches production](testing/test-environment-matches-production.md) — Production code branches on a test flag, an integration test runs on a different storage engine from production, or a test relies on a path, timezone or locale that exists only on one machine.
- [Test inherited methods in each subclass](testing/test-inherited-methods-in-each-subclass.md) — A concrete subclass that adds state or overrides a method its inherited methods call, whose tests exercise only its own new methods while the inherited ones are tested only on the parent instance.
- [The test is the first client of the code](testing/test-is-first-client.md) — A function reads the wall clock, or a test's setup outweighs what it checks: think through the test first and change the signature until that setup disappears. A read of a global is global-data.
- [Test levels](testing/test-levels.md) — Unit, integration, validation and performance tests answer different questions; an integration test re-checking one module's logic, or a failure reproducible in one module with no unit test, shows a level misused.
- [Test scaffolding: stubs, mocks, drivers, dummy files](testing/test-scaffolding.md) — Concept: stand-ins below the unit (stubs, mock objects), drivers above it and small dummy files that isolate the unit under test; the way to test code buried deep in a program or too slow to reach through its callers.
- [Test state coverage, not line coverage](testing/test-state-coverage-not-line-coverage.md) — A function has a divisor, index or length derived from its arguments, its tests reach every line, yet no test input makes that value zero, empty or out of range.
- [When a test suite is good enough](testing/test-suite-adequacy.md) — Concept: a coverage figure offered as proof that a suite is good, or a suite that has to be edited more than the code it tests; neither says whether a defect would make some test fail, which is Fowler's working criterion.
- [A test that verifies nothing](testing/test-that-verifies-nothing.md) — A test only names or constructs a class and asserts nothing, or a later test already covers everything it touches; it adds edits on every rename and no information.
- [Test a module against its contract](testing/test-the-contract.md) — A guard clause or documented precondition has no test that it rejects, a declared limit of the input domain appears in no test input, every test of a unit feeds valid nominal input only, or a module is exercised only through its dependents.
- [Choose test values whose expected result can be checked by hand](testing/test-values-checkable-by-hand.md) — Test inputs like 90783.82 or 1239078382346 next to an expected value nobody can compute in their head, with no derivation shown; pick round values from the same equivalence class.

## Types And State

- [Actor model](types-and-state/actor-model.md) — A lock held across several steps on shared data, with a decision or an outgoing call inside it, is the candidate; in code that claims to use actors, a handler reading another actor's fields, a message carrying a mutable object, or a module variable used from a handler breaks the model.
- [A field's type states the cardinality of its association](types-and-state/association-cardinality-in-field-types.md) — A field for an optional (0..1) association dereferenced at a use site with no absence check, while another site checks it; a to-many association held as a collection that may be null as well as empty, so callers test two kinds of 'none'; or a 1..n collection that a constructor may leave empty or a remove may empty, or a fixed upper bound with no check on add.
- [Automata-Based Programming (Polikarpova, Shalyto)](types-and-state/automata-based-programming.md) — Source page, no rules of its own: a textbook on programming with explicitly separated states, whose pages here own the state-machine shapes in code (history held in flags, a switch that does not mirror the graph, overlapping or missing transitions, control logic mixed with the data it controls, how events reach a machine, how a machine is packaged as a class).
- [Model an entity with complex behaviour as an automated class](types-and-state/automated-class.md) — Clients drive a state machine directly (handle(EVENT), step(e), reading or writing its state field), its control state lives in globals, or a class only wraps one transition routine; repair: one class whose public methods are the events and whose method bodies pick the action by a private control state.
- [Automated object: control automaton plus controlled object](types-and-state/automated-object.md) — Model behind state-machine code: a small automaton holds every 'which action now' decision and the transitions; a controlled object holds the data, is reached only through finite-valued queries and commands, and each command always does the same thing. The shapes that break the split are owned by separate-control-object-from-state-logic (a transition computing inline over the data) and logic-vs-semantics-split (an operation of the controlled object that reads the mode).
- [Avoid type casts](types-and-state/avoid-type-casts.md) — A value is forced from one type into another to get it past the type checker: read back from a generic store (void*, Object, any, an untyped map) and cast to its real type at the point of use, the same cast repeated at several call sites around one interface, or a reinterpretation that silences a reported type error.
- [Called vs nested state machines](types-and-state/called-vs-nested-state-machines.md) — A parent state machine both runs a sub-machine to completion (loop until done, reset first) and steps another or the same one once per tick, or resets a sub-machine on some paths and resumes it on others, with no stated rule on whether it keeps its state across calls.
- [Check-then-act must be atomic](types-and-state/check-then-act-must-be-atomic.md) — `if resource.count > 0` followed by a separate `resource.take()`, or read-modify-write across two calls, on something concurrent code reaches: the value can change between the check and the act.
- [Class invariant](types-and-state/class-invariant.md) — A field bound by a rule is public or has a plain setter, or a getter hands out the mutable collection the rule depends on. A method that can throw between two writes is failure-atomicity.
- [Complex (state-dependent) behaviour](types-and-state/complex-behavior.md) — A handler that does something different for the same input depending on a field earlier inputs set (the same button acts differently by mode) marks complex behaviour, the precondition for replace-flags-with-explicit-states, which decides whether explicit states pay; a handler that does the same thing every call, only on different values, is simple behaviour.
- [Control states and computational states](types-and-state/control-and-computational-states.md) — Telling a variable that selects which action runs (a few named, qualitatively different values, a mode) from one that only holds the result of actions (counters, positions, times): only the first kind becomes explicit states; a mode or phase field mixed among the data fields and tested ad hoc in every routine is the first kind hidden in the second, owned by state-machine-as-switch-on-state (one mode variable) or replace-flags-with-explicit-states (flags).
- [Convert input to its type at the moment of input](types-and-state/convert-input-at-entry.md) — A raw input string such as "yes", "red" or "42" is stored or passed through several routines and compared as text far from where it was read, instead of being parsed into a boolean, enum or number on entry.
- [Decompose a state machine by modes or by controlled objects](types-and-state/decompose-state-machine-by-modes-or-by-controlled-objects.md) — One state enum whose values are products of several independent parts (V1_OPEN_V2_CLOSING, LOCKED_RUNNING_GRILL ...) or copies one part's states per part (V1_OPENING ... V5_OPENING), a state handler carrying a long block of its own sub-phase logic, several state machines identical up to names, or in object-oriented code automata reaching each other through a special nesting mechanism: split by controlled object into classes or instances, or by mode into sub-machines.
- [Declare a named type for each kind of data that may change](types-and-state/define-domain-types.md) — Many declarations of one kind of value (coordinates, employee names, ages) spelled with a built-in type (float, char[30]), a type alias named after its representation (BigInteger, LongString), or an alias that redefines a built-in name.
- [Do not mutate data passed into a function](types-and-state/do-not-mutate-input-data.md) — A function whose job is to compute or prepare data writes fields of a plain record or element it received as an argument (perf.amount = ..., item.play = ...), including inside a map or loop over an input collection; build a copy and enrich the copy instead.
- [Use an enumerated type instead of integer codes and boolean flags](types-and-state/enum-instead-of-codes-and-flags.md) — Integer codes for a closed set of values (kind == 3, 1 = red, 2 = green), a call with several bare true/false arguments, a boolean return value that already needs a third outcome, or two closed sets held in one integer type and mixable.
- [Reserve an invalid first member; beware gaps when iterating an enum](types-and-state/enum-sentinels-and-gaps.md) — An enum whose first (zero) member is a valid value, a loop over an enum by hard-coded first and last members (for c = RED to BLUE), or iteration over an enum whose members have explicit non-consecutive values (1, 2, 4, 8).
- [Event-driven vs polled state machine](types-and-state/event-driven-vs-polled-state-machine.md) — A state machine whose guards test one boolean 'is pressed' flag per button or signal, set and cleared around it, with the same flag guard repeated across states: choose events for discrete happenings and polled inputs for levels.
- [Keep money and other balancing quantities out of floating point](types-and-state/exact-representation-for-money.md) — A monetary amount, or another quantity that must balance to the last unit, held in a float or double with cents as its fractional part, often with round(x, 2) calls scattered after arithmetic to make totals come out right.
- [Externally controlled identifier](types-and-state/externally-controlled-identifier.md) — A phone number, email, postal code, passport or tax number serves as the key of a record or as the reference between records.
- [What a finite automaton cannot do](types-and-state/finite-automaton-limits.md) — A state machine, a set of flags or a regular expression used to track nested or arbitrarily deep structure (brackets, nested blocks, tags closing in reverse order), with depth-limited states such as IN_ONE, IN_TWO: finite control cannot hold unbounded memory or look ahead, so the nesting needs a stack.
- [Finite memory folds into the state set](types-and-state/finite-memory-folds-into-states.md) — A state variable alongside boolean flags or small enums that change what a state does (state = RUNNING plus paused): the real state space is their product, and the flags are unnamed states; only unbounded memory (a count, a stack) cannot be folded in.
- [Finite state machine as a transition table](types-and-state/finite-state-machine.md) — A loop over messages, events or characters sets and tests several boolean flags to track where it is in a sequence; legal orderings are implicit in nested conditionals.
- [Floating values are approximate: no equality, no mixed magnitudes](types-and-state/floating-point-precision.md) — Two floating-point values compared with == or !=, a loop that accumulates a float and tests it for an exact value, a sum that adds a very small value to a very large one, or a fixed absolute epsilon over values of very different scale.
- [Group related data into a structure](types-and-state/group-related-data-into-a-structure.md) — The same run of three or more loose variables or parameters (name, address, phone, ssn...), or a pair that is one domain value (min and max, start and end), is copied, swapped or passed field by field at several sites, with no structure holding them, so adding a field means finding every site and nothing shows which variables belong to which entity.
- [Hybrid coupling](types-and-state/hybrid-coupling.md) — One variable or field whose value ranges carry different meanings: a count where -1 means error, an id where values above a threshold denote a different entity, a size whose negative values hold another quantity.
- [IDs to Objects](types-and-state/ids-to-objects.md) — An identifier (customerId, itemId) entering from input is passed deeper through business methods as a bare number or string and looked up again in several of them, or logic about the thing is written as functions of its id; turn it into the object it names where it enters.
- [Immutable objects](types-and-state/immutable-objects.md) — A method reassigns a field after construction (a setter, in-place arithmetic like `this.x *= f`) instead of returning a new object, or a method mutates an object it received as an argument; fields not final; a setter whose only caller is the constructor.
- [Immutable object versus constant object](types-and-state/immutable-versus-constant-object.md) — A class with only final fields whose methods do I/O or mutate an encapsulated collection is treated as a value: cached, compared, or shared on the assumption that it returns the same answer each time.
- [Initialize close to first use](types-and-state/initialize-close-to-first-use.md) — A variable set at the top of a routine or in a one-off Startup() and first read far below, inside a loop or repeated block that never resets it; a counter or accumulator reused without reset; a value assumed to survive between calls; a read with no initialization visible nearby, though one precedes it on every path.
- [Initialize every data member in every constructor](types-and-state/initialize-every-member-in-every-constructor.md) — A constructor leaves a declared required field unassigned, with no initialiser at its declaration, so the field's value after construction is accidental; or a constructor path sets a field to 0 or empty where a method needs another value (a divisor, an index, a required name), so the object exists in an unusable state.
- [Check integer division, overflow and zero divisors](types-and-state/integer-overflow-and-division.md) — An integer division before a multiplication (10 * (7/10)), a product or sum of integers with no bound on the inputs, an intermediate product that exceeds the type even though the result fits, a division whose divisor can be zero, or an integer compared with a float without an explicit conversion.
- [Interacting state machines: nested, called and pseudo-parallel automata in code](types-and-state/interacting-state-machines.md) — Reference for reading code with several state machines: one step function each, a nested machine stepped once from a parent's action, a called machine looped to its final state, parallel machines stepped in turn from one loop (call order is semantics), active versus passive stepping.
- [Split behaviour between the state machine and the operations it calls](types-and-state/logic-vs-semantics-split.md) — A state machine whose states stand for steps of a computation (SENDING_BYTE_0, SENDING_BYTE_1 ..., one state per digit or index) has primitive operations too low; an operation it calls that itself re-decides control from remembered flags has them too high: move the computation down into a command, or the remembered mode up into a state.
- [Moore, Mealy and mixed machines: where a state machine's outputs live](types-and-state/moore-and-mealy-machines.md) — Reference for where a state machine's actions live: on a state (Moore), on a transition (Mealy) or both (mixed), and whether a transition's action sees the old or the new state.
- [Move a field to the record that changes with it](types-and-state/move-field.md) — A field of record B is passed alongside record A at every call (quote(contract, customer.discountRate)), or a method updating A also writes a field of B to keep them in step, or the same field is updated in several structures at once: move it to the one record it belongs with.
- [Mutable data](types-and-state/mutable-data.md) — Concept: why updating data in place is risky in proportion to its scope, after Fowler's Mutable Data smell; routes each shape (a reused variable, a setter on a field that need not change, a stored derived value, an argument modified in place, a function that both returns and changes state) to the page that owns it.
- [Mutable hash key](types-and-state/mutable-hash-key.md) — An object used as a key in a hash map or set has a mutator called on it after insertion, or its class computes equality and hash from fields that are not final or that hold a mutable container, so the container holds duplicate or unreachable keys.
- [Null object, optional value or exception for absence](types-and-state/null-object-or-optional.md) — An absent value is modelled with a null object none of whose used methods has an honest answer (each throws or returns a made-up value), or with an option type that two or more call sites unwrap with the same default, or that no path returns empty.
- [One variable, one purpose](types-and-state/one-variable-one-purpose.md) — One local variable, often named temp, x, acc or tmp, given two plain assignments (x = ..., not x = x + ...) with values of different meaning in the same routine, such as a discriminant reused as the swap slot or one acceleration overwritten by another; the reuse forces a name that fits neither job.
- [Ownership of nested structures](types-and-state/ownership-of-nested-structures.md) — A container's release routine frees only its top node with no statement about children, or different release sites treat the same children differently.
- [Pass state along instead of hoarding it](types-and-state/pass-state-dont-hoard-it.md) — A field written by one method only for a later method to read; zero-argument void methods that must run in a fixed order, such as one of several parallel ComputeX() calls that also initialises the shared data; objects handing results over by setting each other's fields.
- [How events reach a state machine: global variable, argument, or one function per event](types-and-state/passing-events-to-a-state-machine.md) — An event-driven state machine reads the current event from a global or shared variable that callers must set before calling the step function, or one event is decoded twice, once by the dispatcher choosing the machine and again inside the machine's step function.
- [Plain text for persistent data](types-and-state/plain-text-for-persistent-data.md) — Persisted or exchanged data is written as a binary or fixed-offset layout whose only description is the application code that decodes it.
- [Prefer constant objects](types-and-state/prefer-constant-objects.md) — A class whose state is a final reference to a mutable container changed by its own add/put/remove, filled by a run of such calls straight after new and then passed on, where a copy-returning with() would make it constant.
- [Prefer deep copy unless shallow is proven necessary](types-and-state/prefer-deep-copy.md) — A copy constructor or clone assigns the original's mutable reference fields to the copy (often with reference counting or 'still shared' checks around it), with no measurement in view justifying the sharing; or, the reverse, a copy deep-copies immutable values or independent entities such as a shared customer.
- [Replace behaviour flags with one explicit control-state variable](types-and-state/replace-flags-with-explicit-states.md) — Two or more boolean or small-range fields of one entity, tested in combination by several of its own input handlers to pick a different reaction to the same input (alarm_on and setting_alarm, lampOn and wasPressed): an implicit state machine; name the modes, hold them in one state variable, give each handler one case per state.
