- [Replace an overloaded primitive with a class](types-and-state/replace-primitive-with-class.md) — Two different quantities (money and temperature, a price and a quantity, ids of two different entities) share one bare int, float or string type, so assigning, adding or comparing one with the other compiles; or one domain value held as a primitive whose range or format check, comparison or formatting (priority == "high" or "rush", slicing an area code out of a phone string) is written out again at several use sites.
- [A representation that fits only by coincidence](types-and-state/representation-that-fits-by-coincidence.md) — A phone number or identifier in a numeric field, key-value pairs in an array searched by first match, a fixed conversion between units whose size depends on place, or a bare quantity with no unit.
- [Separate the control object from the state logic](types-and-state/separate-control-object-from-state-logic.md) — A state machine's step function or state classes compute over the controlled data inline (time arithmetic, compound comparisons of several fields, device fiddling) instead of calling named queries and commands, the same compound guard repeated across states, or control-object members named after automaton ids such as x1 or z5.
- [Shared state is incorrect state](types-and-state/shared-state-is-incorrect-state.md) — A thread or task body, or a callback handed to a scheduler, pool or event loop, touches a variable or object captured from outside, two tasks receive the same mutable object, or concurrent code temporarily changes process-wide state such as the current directory: each works from a view it cannot guarantee is current.
- [Spontaneous and guarded transitions](types-and-state/spontaneous-and-guarded-transitions.md) — A state machine whose transitions fire on the machine's own initiative after checking a condition, or a flowchart turned into states: guards on a diagram are checked at once, while an if/else-if chain checks them in order and silently resolves overlaps by line order.
- [Group states that share an outgoing transition](types-and-state/state-grouping-for-shared-transitions.md) — The same transition (same condition, same action, same target state, e.g. `if estop: close(); state = FAULT`) copied into the case arms of several states of one state machine: write it once as a group transition.
- [Implement a state machine as a switch on the state with one guarded branch per transition](types-and-state/state-machine-as-switch-on-state.md) — Code that holds a mode in a state variable but does not mirror the transition graph: inputs tested first and the state inside, the state assigned in several places or outside the step function, or a selection over every combination of inputs where one or two decide; no block of code corresponds to one state or one transition.
- [State machine, event stream or publish-subscribe](types-and-state/state-machine-or-event-stream-or-pubsub.md) — A state machine with states counting events plus timestamp fields, or a stream used only to fan out: pick the tool by what must be remembered.
- [Table or switch: choose a state machine's representation by whether it changes at run time](types-and-state/state-machine-table-or-switch.md) — A transition table assembled at start-up for a state machine that never changes afterwards, a state machine hard-coded as a switch although its states or transitions are loaded or edited while the program runs, or a transition table indexed by the full vector of boolean inputs.
- [State machines communicate through an explicit interface](types-and-state/state-machines-communicate-through-an-explicit-interface.md) — One state machine's guard reads another machine's raw state number or enum (`if valveA.state == 3`, `a2.y != 1`), or a flag field sits in shared data only to signal between machines: name each dependence as a predicate the owner exposes, then replace it with an event.
- [Status variable as an enumeration behind an accessor](types-and-state/status-variable-as-enumeration.md) — A status or error state is a boolean (isError, ok, failed), or several booleans for one state, tested directly by several functions outside the code that sets it, so a third state or a combined condition means revisiting every test.
- [Stored derived data](types-and-state/stored-derived-data.md) — A field whose value is computable from other fields of the same structure, a setter that must recompute a second field to keep the two in step, or one method that both records a fact and adjusts a stored summary of the facts (adjustments.add(a); production += a.amount).
- [Switch on state vs the State pattern](types-and-state/switch-on-state-vs-state-pattern.md) — Every event method of a class opens with a switch over the same control-state field, one case per state, so one state's behaviour is scattered across methods; or a class per state, per event and per transition for a machine never changed at run time: choose between the switch, the State pattern, and tables.
- [Test a value by its kind](types-and-state/test-a-value-by-its-kind.md) — A boolean held as an integer 0/1 or compared to true/false (flag = 1, done == false), or a number or reference used bare as a condition (while balance, if ptr): use a boolean or an enum, test booleans directly, compare numbers and references explicitly.
- [Transitions of a state machine: every state reachable, conditions from one state consistent and complete](types-and-state/transition-conditions-consistent-and-complete.md) — In one state's handler, two branches whose conditions can both be true at once (outcome decided silently by textual order or by which assignment runs last), a branch chain with no fallback so some input falls through with no defined transition, a fallback spelled as the negation of every other condition, or a state value that no transition ever assigns.
- [Variable state anomalies](types-and-state/variable-state-anomalies.md) — On one path a variable is assigned twice with no read between, assigned and never read before return or release, read after its resource was freed or closed, freed twice, or a local is read before any assignment.
